articles.title: Female Basij commander shot by assassins in south-eastern Iran
articles.summary: An officer commanding a women's unit in Iran's Basij paramilitary force has been shot and killed outside her home in the Mehrestan district of Iran's Sistan-...
articles.body:
An officer commanding a women's unit in Iran's Basij paramilitary force has been shot and killed outside her home in the Mehrestan district of Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan Province, the Tasnim news agency reported on Wednesday.

Another officer was killed in a separate attack on a police vehicle in Mehrestan in the province which lies in south-eastern Iran and borders Pakistan and Afghanistan.

The volunteer Basij militia is subordinate to the Islamic Republican Guard Corps (IGRC), to which Tasnim is linked.

Clashes between Iranian security forces and militant groups have been reported in the province in recent days. Several people have been killed, according to the reports. The death tolls cannot be independently verified.

Iran's military leadership has described the incidents as targeted attacks intended to destabilize the south-east and undermine national stability. It blames its adversaries - Israel and the United States - accusing them of supporting separatists and militant groups.

Meanwhile, concerns are mounting in Iran over a new military campaign and airstrikes in the country.

On Wednesday, the human rights group Haalvash, which reports on the border province, said the security situation remained tense in several locations. It reported that military helicopters were circling over the city of Iranshahr.

articles.title: Daniel Santos anuncia equipe de transição; veja nomes | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo vai levantar informações administrativas, financeiras e operacionais do Estado. Ofício foi encaminhado à governadora Hana Ghassan.
articles.summary: Grupo vai levantar informações administrativas, financeiras e operacionais do Estado. Ofício foi encaminhado à governadora Hana Ghassan.
articles.body:
O governador eleito no Pará Dr Daniel Santos ( Podemos ) anunciou, nesta quinta-feira (15), a composição de uma equipe de transição. O grupo vai levantar informações administrativas, financeiras e operacionais do Estado.

Segundo a assessoria do governador eleito , um ofício também foi encaminhando à atual governadora do Pará, Hana Ghassan ( MDB ), solicitando o início dos trabalhos.

O objetivo da equipe é garantir uma transferência administrativa organizada, transparente e responsável, segundo o anúncio.

Ainda de acordo com a assessoria do governador eleito, os nomes dos integrantes é exclusiva para o processo de transição. No entanto, um dos integrantes dessa equipe, Viniciu Borba, já foi anunciado por Daniel como secretário de Meio Ambiente da sua gestão.

Confira abaixo os nomes dos integrantes da equipe de transição de governo:

João Luís Brasil Batista Rolim de Castro

Grace de Nazareth Rodrigues Soares Ramalho

Empresas públicas, sociedades de economia mista, fundações e autarquias

Dr. Daniel (Podemos) foi eleito governador do Pará no primeiro turno das eleições de 2026, em 4 de outubro. A eleição foi matematicamente definida por volta das 21h, com 97,46% das urnas apuradas.

articles.title: EUA planejam usar a 'mãe de todas as bombas' contra o Irã | G1
articles.standfirst: Planos incluem a bomba GBU-43/B, mas autoridades americanas questionam sua eficácia para atingir os objetivos estratégicos de Washington, segundo a CNN Internacional.
articles.summary: As Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos elaboraram planos de ataque contra instalações nucleares e a infraestrutura energética do Irã que podem incluir a bomba GBU-43/B, segundo a CNN
articles.body:
A "mãe de todas as bombas" é um explosivo convencional de 9,8 toneladas guiado por GPS e tem potência equivalente a cerca de 11 toneladas de TNT. — Foto: Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos / AFP

As Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos elaboraram planos de ataque contra o Irã que podem usar a bomba GBU-43/B, conhecida como “mãe de todas as bombas” . A informação foi divulgada pela CNN Internacional nesta quinta-feira (15), com base em relatos de autoridades americanas.

Os alvos seriam instalações nucleares e a infraestrutura energética do país. Os ataques poderiam ocorrer caso o presidente Donald Trump ordene a retomada das operações militares.

O uso da maior bomba não nuclear do arsenal americano representaria uma escalada significativa do conflito. Ainda há dúvidas, porém, sobre a eficácia da arma para atingir os objetivos estratégicos de Washington, segundo autoridades ouvidas pela rede de televisão americana.

O apelido do explosivo, “mãe de todas as bombas” (Mother of All Bombs, no inglês original), vem da sigla MOAB. O acrônimo, por sua vez, significa Massive Ordnance Air Blast, ou explosão aérea de munição de grande porte.

A arma pesa cerca de 9,8 toneladas e tem aproximadamente nove metros de comprimento. Sua potência explosiva equivale a cerca de 11 toneladas de TNT. Apesar do poder de destruição, ela não se compara às bombas nucleares usadas pelos Estados Unidos contra Hiroshima e Nagasaki, no Japão, em 1945.

A MOAB foi testada pela primeira vez em março de 2003, na Flórida. A bomba é guiada por GPS e foi projetada para ser lançada de aeronaves militares de transporte, como o MC-130, com auxílio de um paraquedas.

Desenvolvida por Albert L. Weimorts Jr., do Laboratório de Pesquisa da Força Aérea americana, a arma foi projetada para atingir alvos em uma grande área com uma onda de choque intensa.

Os Estados Unidos decidiram suspender os ataques contra alvos iranianos até o fim das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato — as midterms, marcadas para 3 de novembro.

Em uma publicação no começo de outubro , o presidente do país, Donald Trump , descartou novos ataques contra o país persa até o final do mês e disse que Washington e Teerã estão tendo “discussões produtivas”.

“Quero deixar claro para todos que, embora o Irã esteja em péssimas condições, tanto econômica quanto militarmente, e embora o bloqueio permaneça em pleno vigor e efeito, (...) não atacaremos o Irã em nenhum momento antes das eleições de meio de mandato que serão realizadas nos Estados Unidos ”.

Depois da publicação do presidente, o Tesouro dos EUA anunciou novas sanções contra o Irã , visando dezenas de pessoas, entidades e embarcações.

Apesar da suspensão dos ataques, não há nenhum acordo de trégua vigente entre os países.

articles.title: Baiana é alvo de ação civil após dizer na web que LGBT não é normal | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher foi denunciada por LGBTfobia. Defensoria Pública do Estado (DOE) pede vídeo com retratação na web e indenização por dano moral coletivo de R$ 30 mil.
articles.summary: Mulher foi denunciada por LGBTfobia. Defensoria Pública do Estado (DOE) pede vídeo com retratação na web e indenização por dano moral coletivo de R$ 30 mil
articles.body:
Uma empresária da cidade de Santo Antônio de Jesus , no Recôncavo Baiano, virou alvo de uma ação civil pública após compartilhar nas redes sociais um vídeo com falas consideradas LGBTfóbicas.

A informação foi divulgada pela Defensoria Pública do Estado da Bahia (DPE/BA), que acionou a Justiça depois de uma denúncia de um coletivo LGBTQIAPN+ da região. Foram pedidos um vídeo com retratação e o pagamento indenização por dano moral coletivo de R$ 30 mil.

Na publicação, Day Souza relata uma experiência com a filha, uma criança que teria questionado o que é ser LGBT. Segundo a empresária, na resposta, ela afirmou que é algo que não pode ser considerado normal.

"Para responder, eu falei o seguinte: 'Filha, então... tem coisas que o mundo vai querer trazer para gente como o normal, mas a Bíblia diz que Deus criou Adão e Eva. Deus criou o homem e a Mulher. Deus criou um para o outro. Então, assim como mamãe é casada com papai, lá na frente, Deus vai preparar um príncipe para você casar. E foi isso que Deus criou", contou.

Bandeira LGBT - LGBTQIA+ — Foto: Sophie Emeny/Unsplash

A empresária contou ainda que uma prima da criança estava na conversa e que ela teria tocado no assunto primeiro, porque já sabia o significado.

"Lembrando que todas as minhas sobrinhas, para honra e glória do Senhor, também são cristãs. A maior já sabia o que significava, só que ela não", explicou.

Por fim, a baiana alegou ter pedido à filha que sempre buscasse ajuda com dúvidas como essas. "Sempre que a gente tiver essas dúvidas, a gente vai perguntar, não para qualquer pessoa".

O g1 tentou, mas não tinha conseguido contato com a mulher até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Em nota, o defensor público Daniel Bernardes, que atua no caso, disse que a ação não discute fé e nem liberdade religiosa, mas a divulgação pública de uma fala que inferioriza um grupo social.

“A posição da Defensoria Pública enquanto instituição é de que discursos de ódio não são protegidos pela Constituição. Esses discursos não estão dentro da liberdade religiosa, da liberdade de expressão e não é algo que se deseje que seja empregado na orientação dos filhos pelos pais”, explicou.

Ainda conforme o órgão, antes de ajuizar uma ação civil pública, foi feita uma recomendação da retirada do vídeo do ar, com a publicação de uma retratação também em vídeo. A empresária removeu a publicação e divulgou uma nota escrita, mas não gravou a retratação.

“Embora haja o pedido de indenização, o principal objetivo da ação é a retratação. Isso se deve ao caráter pedagógico da medida, à necessidade de educação em direitos da população, inclusive das pessoas que sustentam esse discurso LGBTfóbico”, afirmou o defensor.

articles.title: Profissões da área da saúde: formação prática e impacto social | G1
articles.standfirst: Na Asces-Unita, estudantes da área da Saúde têm acesso a uma formação prática e conectada à realidade, com experiências que também geram impacto social.
articles.summary: A formação em profissões da área da saúde na Asces-Unita integra prática acadêmica e impacto social por meio de atendimentos gratuitos à comunidade.
articles.body:
Escolher uma profissão na área da Saúde é também descobrir diferentes formas de cuidar, acolher e transformar vidas. Na série Com Que Curso Eu Vou?, a Asces-Unita apresenta diferentes áreas de formação e mostra as possibilidades que podem fazer parte da trajetória profissional dos estudantes.

No quarto episódio, o destaque é para o Eixo Saúde. Thais percorre os corredores dos laboratórios do Campus II e conversa com o professor Paulo Gustavo, sobre Medicina, e com a professora Danila, sobre Psicologia, mostrando que o cuidado com as pessoas envolve uma rede completa de profissionais.

O episódio também destaca um dos diferenciais da formação na Asces-Unita: o impacto social proporcionado pelas clínicas-escola, que oferecem atendimentos gratuitos à população e aproximam os estudantes da prática profissional.

Para quem tem vocação para cuidar de vidas, são diferentes caminhos e possibilidades de formação. Com que curso você vai?

articles.title: Batida entre trem e ônibus na entrada do Eurotúnel deixa 19 feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (15), segundo autoridades locais. Imprensa francesa afirma que cinco pessoas sofreram ferimentos graves.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (15), segundo autoridades locais. Imprensa francesa afirma que cinco pessoas sofreram ferimentos graves.
articles.body:
Trem de alta velocidade TGV TMST na saída do Eurotúnel, em Coquelles, na França, em 20 de agosto de 2014 — Foto: Billy69150/Wikimedia Commons

Uma colisão entre um trem de carga e um ônibus deixou 19 feridos na França nesta quinta-feira (15), segundo autoridades locais. O acidente aconteceu na entrada do Eurotúnel, que liga o país ao Reino Unido por baixo do Canal da Mancha.

Segundo a emissora francesa BFM TV, cinco dos feridos estão em estado crítico. Equipes de emergência foram enviadas ao local, assim como um helicóptero.

O Eurotúnel tem cerca de 50 km de extensão e abriga uma ligação ferroviária submarina entre a França e o Reino Unido. Carros e ônibus também atravessam o túnel, mas não de forma convencional. Os veículos são transportados por trens especiais.

Incidentes no Eurotúnel são extremamente incomuns. Em 1996 e 2008, incêndios em trens que faziam a travessia deixaram passageiros feridos, mas não houve mortes. Nas duas ocasiões, o túnel ficou fechado ou teve o tráfego parcialmente suspenso por alguns dias.

O acidente desta quinta-feira aconteceu cerca de um mês após o descarrilamento de um trem com quase 200 passageiros no norte da França. Na ocasião, mais de 40 pessoas ficaram feridas . As autoridades abriram uma investigação e apuram a hipótese de sabotagem.

articles.title: Conservatório Pernambucano de Música abre seleção com 165 vagas | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições seguem até 23 de outubro, pela internet. Oportunidades são para aulas de instrumentos e formação musical.
articles.summary: Inscrições seguem até 23 de outubro, pela internet. Oportunidades são para aulas de instrumentos e formação musical.
articles.body:
Conservatório Pernambucano de Música abre inscrições para cursos — Foto: Elton Campos/Divulgação

O Conservatório Pernambucano de Música (CPM) está com 165 vagas para cursos técnicos em Canto, Composição e Arranjo, Regência e Instrumento Musical. As inscrições seguem até 23 de outubro, pela internet , e são gratuitas.

As oportunidades são para candidatos com conhecimento musical teórico e prático de nível intermediário. No momento da inscrição, o candidato deve escolher apenas um curso. O processo seletivo conta com provas prática e teórica, que vão ser aplicadas em dezembro.

As vagas estão distribuídas entre os turnos da manhã, tarde e noite, na unidade do CPM que fica no bairro de Santo Amaro, no Centro do Recife . As aulas para os selecionados começam no dia 11 de fevereiro de 2027.

Os cursos contemplam diferentes instrumentos, como violão, guitarra, violoncelo, percussão, bateria, oboé, tuba e trombone. Além disso, também há oportunidade para Canto Erudito.

Os candidatos ao curso de Canto Erudito devem passar por uma triagem antes de realizar as provas teórica e prática. A análise prévia será por meio do envio de um vídeo executando peças determinadas no edital .

Para efetuar a matrícula, os selecionados pelas provas teórica e prática deverão estar cursando ou já ter concluído o ensino médio. A matrícula dos aprovados será realizada no dia 14 de dezembro, de forma presencial.

articles.title: Missa e escultura marcam evento pelos 35 anos da visita do papa a MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Celebração será nesta sexta-feira (16), no Sesi Papa, com entrada gratuita e expectativa de reunir 4 mil fiéis. Programação começa às 19h e inclui apresentação de Celina Borges.
articles.summary: Celebração será nesta sexta-feira (16), no Sesi Papa, com entrada gratuita e expectativa de reunir 4 mil fiéis. Programação começa às 19h e inclui apresentação de Celina Borges.
articles.body:
Papa João Paulo II em visita a Cuiabá — Foto: TV Centro América

Cuiabá recebe nesta sexta-feira (16) uma celebração pelos 35 anos da visita do papa João Paulo II à capital mato-grossense. O evento será realizado no Sesi Papa, na região da Cruz do Papa, local onde o pontífice celebrou uma missa em 1991. A expectativa é reunir cerca de 4 mil pessoas. A entrada é gratuita.

A programação começa às 19h, com uma missa. Às 20h, será inaugurada uma escultura do papa, produzida pelo escultor Francisco Charneca. O evento termina às 21h, com um show da cantora católica Celina Borges.

A celebração relembra a passagem de João Paulo II por Cuiabá, em outubro de 1991, quando o pontífice se encontrou com fiéis e jovens de diferentes regiões do país. A visita marcou a história religiosa da capital mato-grossense.

🕗 20h: Inauguração da nova escultura de São João Paulo II, assinada pelo artista Francisco Charneca

📍 Local: Sesi Papa – Avenida Oátomo Canavarros, s/n, Morada do Ouro, em frente ao Atacadão.

🎟️ Entrada gratuita e sem necessidade de inscrição!

Em 16 de outubro de 1991, o papa João Paulo II se reuniu com mais de 4,5 mil jovens de diferentes regiões do país, em Cuiabá . A recepção ao pontífice foi marcada pela emoção de fiéis que se aproximaram para cumprimentá-lo.

Durante o discurso, o papa abordou a situação dos imigrantes e demonstrou preocupação com as condições de vida das crianças. Segundo ele, elas estavam entre as principais vítimas da migração descontrolada, expostas à miséria, à delinquência, ao abandono e à precariedade.

A proteção ambiental também esteve entre os temas tratados pelo pontífice. Ele destacou a relação entre a preservação da natureza e o direito fundamental à vida. João Paulo II ainda alertou para a exploração desordenada dos recursos naturais e afirmou que a busca por ganhos materiais muitas vezes se sobrepunha a valores essenciais.

articles.title: No Dia dos Professores, educadores precisam atravessar rio para dar aula em cidade ilhada pelas chuvas no PR | G1
articles.standfirst: Rios da região acabaram saindo do curso e inundaram as estradas de acesso ao município. DER-PR diz que volume do rio na cidade está baixando, mas não o suficiente para o tráfego nos pontos alagados.
articles.summary: Rios da região acabaram saindo do curso e inundaram as estradas de acesso ao município.
articles.body:
Moradores de Mirador , no Noroeste do Paraná, precisaram usar um barco para chegar e sair do município nesta quinta-feira (15).

Por conta da cheia do Rio Ivaí, outros rios da região acabaram saindo do curso e inundaram a PR-559 e PR-180, estradas que dão acesso à cidade. A embarcação está sendo oferecida pela prefeitura da cidade.

À RPC, afiliada da TV Globo, a professora Regina Soares, educadora da rede estadual, relatou que, em outros momentos, os moradores também tiveram que fazer o trajeto dessa maneira por conta dos alagamentos.

"Esse é o obstáculo que a gente enfrenta para atender nossos alunos. A gente enfrentou fazer esse trajeto de barco outras vezes e estamos aqui novamente. Não tem o que fazer, são forças da natureza", disse Regina.

Outra alternativa para chegar ao município é o distrito de Quatro Marcos, mas, por conta do alto volume de chuva, a estrada está em situações precárias.

De acordo com a prefeitura de Mirador, o transporte de barco continuará durante o dia. Após a chuva cessar na região, a prioridade será em ajustes na estrada de Quatro Marcos, para evitar novos transtornos.

O Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem do Paraná (DER-PR) informou que, na tarde desta quinta-feira, o volume do rio na cidade está baixando, mas não o suficiente para o tráfego nos pontos alagados.

Conforme o Climatempo, Mirador deve registrar pancadas de chuvas no período da noite. O volume acumulado previsto para o dia é de 4,6 milímetros.

articles.title: At least 5 killed in Houthi attack on Yemen’s presidential palace in Aden
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition accuses Houthis of obtaining missile parts from regional states.
articles.body:
At least five people have been killed in the vicinity of the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Yemen’s port city of Aden after Houthi missile strikes.

Yemeni health minister says five people were killed and 16 others injured in the Houthi missile attack that targeted the al-Maashiq Presidential Palace in Yemen’s Aden on Thursday.

The Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said in a social media post on Thursday that Houthis had targeted the al-Maashiq presidential palace with five missiles.

The government says the prime minister and other officials are safe, but two of his bodyguards were killed in the attack.

Plumes of smoke could be seen rising from the vicinity of the palace.

Al Jazeera correspondents reported earlier on Thursday that there were explosions near the palace.

The palace is considered the headquarters and the seat of power for the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government.

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, said the attacks on the headquarters of the internationally recognised government are the “first of their kind” by the Houthis.

“This is an indication that the escalation is going to intensify between both sides,” Mawry said, adding that fears are now growing inside the country of “an all-out civil war” that could potentially drag in other regional powers besides Saudi Arabia.

The attack in Aden came as fighting between the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), and Saudi-backed forces intensified in Taiz, which is effectively under siege by the Houthis.

Controlling Taiz, Yemen’s third city and the broader Taiz governorate, in the southwest of the country would ensure control over the critical Bab al-Mandeb strait for either side.

Forces allied with the Yemeni government said they are repelling a Houthi attack on Dhubab airport.

The pro-government Homeland Shield Force said in a statement that they are, along with the Southern Giants Brigades, securing the airport in the coastal city of Dhubab in Taiz governorate.

Aid agencies say the escalating violence in Taiz is pushing the healthcare system towards breaking point.

On Sunday, the Ministry of Public Health warned of a “humanitarian catastrophe” there.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition says Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport has come under at least 20 Houthi attacks over the past 11 days with dozens of other airports, oil facilities and ports also targeted.

Major-General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the alliance, released footage showing strikes on the main airport with passengers seen fleeing for safety, during a news conference in the Saudi capital

The coalition says the Houthi attacks have killed 17 people and injured more than 300.

Al-Maliki also accused the Houthis of obtaining ballistic missiles from other countries in the region.

Mohamad Elmasry, a professor at the Doha Institute for Graduate Studies, said the Saudi-led coalition’s news conference was intended as a response “to some of the, perhaps, military and security failures”.

“There’s kind of an image problem there because this is maybe affecting the perception of Saudi deterrence, the fact that missiles are getting through,” he told Al Jazeera.

Elmasry said the Houthis also have an image crisis, with the global community viewing their actions as “reprehensible, in particular these targeting civilian infrastructure”.

articles.summary: I learned the best products for cleaning and polishing wood furniture, including wood tables, cabinets, chairs and more.
articles.body: I know all about how to clean hardwood floors, but when it came to cleaning and polishing wood chairs, cabinetry, consoles and tables, I realized I had a lot to learn. I’ve done some light dusting around my apartment with my favorite kits, but I needed to reach out to cleaning experts to learn more about the best way to clean and polish wood furniture. The most important thing I took away from the experts, including Becky Rapinchuk, owner of cleaning brand and site Clean Mama, is that the same polish you’d use for floors isn’t necessarily compatible with wood furniture. “Floor products are formulated differently and may contain waxes, silicones, or leave a slippery residue that isn’t intended for furniture surfaces,” she says. “It’s generally best to use products designed for the specific surface.” To find the right products and methods for polishing wood furniture, I asked Rapinchuk and another cleaning expert for their recommendations. They also provide tips for polishing finished and sealed wood furniture in just a few easy steps. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for polishing wood furniture Below are products recommended by our experts or staff, and/or are highly rated on Amazon with at least a 4-star average from 500 or more shoppers. I’ve used this duster kit from Swiffer multiple times to clean around my home, including my wood television stand and corners of my wood floors, and it works incredibly well. It includes a handle and five refills dusters that slide onto the handle easily. I love them because they do such a great job of grabbing — not pushing around — the dust, so much so that I don’t even see dust flying in the air like with other dusters. This kit has a short handle, but there’s also a version with a 3-foot handle and fluffier duster that’s also popular. “For polishing, use a quality wood polish (I like beeswax) or conditioner sparingly, applying it with a soft cloth and buffing in the direction of the grain,” says Rapinchuk. This polish not only makes wood furniture shiny, but it also restores the moisture and vibrancy of the wood, since it’s also a conditioner. It helps get rid of things like fading and weathering on wood furniture, according to the brand. Some shoppers say it does a great job of disguising some scratches on wood furniture. To use the polish, which has a honey-like consistency, put a small amount of it on a microfiber cloth, and apply it to the wood. Allow it to sit for 20 minutes before wiping any excess polish from the surface. This spray is made for cleaning and shining wood furniture like cabinets, baseboards, doors, chairs, and even finished antiques (and painted wood), according to the brand. It gets rid of dust and debris on the surface of the wood, adds shine and leaves a protective layer on the surface. Plus, the spray helps prevent water marks and grease, according to the brand and shoppers. Some people who bought it also say that they also enjoy the almond scent it has. The set comes with a microfiber cloth, which Rapinchuk recommends using for cleaning. This beeswax-based polish works like the liquid polish above, but it has a balm consistency. Apply a small dollop of it to a cloth and buff it into wood furniture in a circular motion. It helps make the furniture shiny but not greasy, according to shoppers. Some also say that it works well for conditioning wood furniture that has a dry appearance. It’s made with food-grade ingredients, including olive oil (in addition to beeswax), so you could also technically use it on wooden utensils, according to the brand. Ryan Knoll, owner of home cleaning company TidyCasa, says he likes to use products from Pledge, which is well-known for its products for cleaning and polishing wood. Shoppers say the wipes help get rid of dust but also make wood shiny without feeling greasy. Start by using a duster attached to a dusting wand, such as from a Swiffer Duster Starter Kit, and gently glide it along the surface of the furniture, making sure to collect as much dust as possible. You may also have to use a dusting sponge, such as the Mr.Scrub Damp Dusting Sponge, to clean dust from crevices. Use a lightly damp microfiber cloth, like the Homexcel Microfiber Cloths, to wipe away any residual dust and debris on the furniture.Apply a small amount of beeswax-based wood polish and conditioner, such as the Rhoose Natural Beeswax Polish for Wood & Furniture or the Howard Beeswax Wood Polish & Conditioner to a microfiber cloth, according to the directions. Wipe the polish into the finished and sealed wood furniture with circular motions, making sure to cover all sealed and finished surfaces of the furniture. As an alternative, apply a wood polish spray, such as the Weiman Cabinet & Wood Cleaner and Protectant Spray or a wipe like Pledge Expert Care Wood Wipes to clean and polish the furniture.Allow the polish to dry, according to the directions, and use another soft cloth to wipe any excess polish from the surface. articles.title: US midterms: Trump warns voters Democrats will 'destroy' America, backs Andy Biggs in Arizona governor race
articles.summary: In a rally in Bullhead City, President Trump urged Arizona voters to support Republican candidates, attacking Democrats and endorsing gubernatorial candidate Andy Biggs. He emphasized the importance of voting in memory of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, and criticized Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs. Trump revisited his State of the Union address, calling for protection of American citizens over undocumented immigrants, and praised various Republican candidates across the state.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump urged Arizona voters to support Republican candidates in the November elections, attacking Democrats over their response to his State of the Union address and backing Rep. Andy Biggs in the race for governor.Speaking at a rally in Bullhead City on Wednesday, Trump criticised Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs and called on Republicans to win elections across the state. He also urged supporters to vote in memory of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.“On election night, Arizona is going to prove that America does not belong to those who hate it,” Trump said. “America belongs to those who love, love, love, love, love it.”Biggs, the Republican gubernatorial nominee, called on the crowd to support the party’s candidates across the ballot.“Vote Republican top to bottom,” he said. “Let’s turn Arizona red.”Trump revisits State of the Union confrontationTrump’s criticism of Democrats centred on their response to his February 24 State of the Union address, when he challenged lawmakers to affirm that the government’s first responsibility was to protect American citizens rather than undocumented immigrants.Republicans stood in response, while many Democrats remained seated. Trump returned to the episode at Wednesday’s rally, accusing Democrats of failing to acknowledge veterans and other guests recognised during the speech.“Not one Democrat smiled or clapped,” he said. “And that’s when I looked at them, and I said, ‘You people are crazy.’”“But that’s what we have,” Trump added. “They’ll destroy our country.”During the speech, the President awarded the Medal of Honour to retired Navy Capt. E. Royce Williams, who was 100 at the time, and recognised World War II veteran George “Buddy” Taggart. The confrontation over standing occurred during a separate appeal for lawmakers to prioritise the protection of American citizens.Democratic Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania said he stood to recognise the honoured guests, including veterans.Trump also attacked Hobbs personally, describing the governor as a “low IQ individual”. Biggs is seeking to unseat her in the election.Trump urges support for Republican candidatesThe rally featured several other Republican candidates seeking office in Arizona. Trump endorsed Sine Kerr, a former state senator selected by Biggs in July as his running mate for the newly created position of lieutenant governor.He also backed Republican secretary of state candidate Alex Kolodin, calling him “a warrior for election integrity” while criticising Democratic incumbent Adrian Fontes.Trump praised Republican Reps. Paul Gosar, Abe Hamadeh and Eli Crane, describing Hamadeh and Crane as “warriors”. He also urged voters to support congressional candidate Mark Lamb in Arizona’s 5th Congressional District, calling him a friend.The event included a tribute to Kirk, whom Trump said would have turned 33 on Wednesday. The president described the conservative activist as “a great person, a great man, a great friend of mine”, as supporters chanted his name.Trump also expressed support for Kirk’s widow, Erika, and their family before urging voters to make the election a tribute to the activist.“In Charlie’s honour, we want you to go out and vote,” Trump said. “He’d be out there fighting like nobody else. So, let’s have a big victory in honour of Charlie Kirk.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kamala Harris slams Biden & Trump over Gaza war, says US should have acted ‘sooner, more forcefully’
articles.summary: Former US vice president Kamala Harris has criticised both the Joe Biden and Donald Trump administrations for failing to use Washington’s influence to
articles.body: Former US vice president Kamala Harris has criticised both the Joe Biden and Donald Trump administrations for failing to use Washington’s influence to control Israel’s military campaign in Gaza, saying the US should have acted “sooner and more forcefully”.Speaking at the Asan Memorial Lecture organised by the Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Harris described the failure to use American leverage to curb the Israeli government’s conduct during the war in Gaza as a major shortcoming of US policy.“Most recently, the failure to use our leverage to curtail the Israeli government’s horrific conduct in the war in Gaza, both under the current administration, which offers [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu a blank check, and our administration before, where we should have acted sooner and more forcefully,” Harris said.Her remarks amounted to a criticism of the Biden administration, under which she served as vice president, as well as the current Trump administration, which she accused of giving Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unconditional support.Republican Jewish Coalition hits back at HarrisHarris’s comments drew criticism from the Republican Jewish Coalition, which described her position as “unsurprising”. The group cited her absence from Netanyahu’s 2024 address to the US Congress and her opposition to legislation targeting the boycott, divestment and sanctions (BDS) movement against Israel.The organisation also criticised Harris for calling for a halt to Israeli military operations in Rafah, a city in southern Gaza, and for agreeing with a student in 2021 who accused Israel of “ethnic genocide”.Warren Kinsella, an attorney and author who worked on Harris’s 2024 presidential campaign, also expressed disappointment over her latest remarks, writing on social media that he was “ashamed to have worked with her”.Harris says US foreign policy needs a rethinkBeyond the Gaza conflict, Harris spoke about the changing nature of American power and the need to rethink traditional approaches to foreign policy.She argued that economic innovation, markets, minerals and semiconductor technology were becoming increasingly important sources of global influence, alongside military strength.“Coming out of world wars, and into the Cold War, military might was the primary source of power,” she said. “But now more than ever, economic innovation, markets and minerals, chips and computers, have greater influence.”Harris also stressed the importance of strengthening US alliances, pointing to closer ties among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea as a development Washington and its partners needed to monitor.Harris puts 2026 midterms ahead of 2028 presidential raceHarris expressed confidence that Democrats would win the November 2026 midterm elections but sidestepped a direct question about whether she planned to run for president in 2028.“2028, from my perspective, doesn’t matter if we don’t win 2026,” she said, indicating that the immediate priority for Democrats was the upcoming congressional elections.You use AI every day. articles.title: Andy Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected
articles.summary: The prime minister had faced calls to apologise for his comments about the alleged murder of the former minister.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has asked for Parliament's official record to be corrected after telling MPs an "individual" was "responsible for the murder" of Ann Widdecombe.

The prime minister had faced calls to apologise for the remarks, made during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday, with a senior Tory saying they breached the "presumption of innocence" in criminal cases.

A man was charged with Widdecombe's murder in July, but is yet to enter a plea for the charge and is not due to stand trial until next year.

A No 10 spokeswoman said a correction had been issued to Hansard, the official report of parliamentary debates, and would be "published in due course".

Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform spokeswoman.

A trial before a High Court judge is scheduled for 8 June next year, and a plea and case management hearing on 29 January.

Earlier this month, Kerry was also charged with preparing acts of terror including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Speaking on Thursday, Conservative shadow Commons leader Jesse Norman accused Burnham of breaching Parliament's sub judice rule, which says MPs should not refer to pending court cases in order to avoid influencing the outcome.

He added that the prime minister's comments at PMQs had "breached the legal presumption of innocence".

He asked Commons leader Sir Alan Campbell, a government minister, to "correct the record, withdraw the remark and apologise on behalf of the prime minister".

In response, Sir Alan said the prime minister had "said that he misspoke, he has apologised and he has corrected the record".

"There is no excuse for misspeaking in the House and I am not trying to explain that away, but this prime minister is characterised by an authenticity and a passion in the way that he responds," he added.

"It is not unusual for prime ministers or anybody else to misspeak in the House.

"As long as they correct the record, which he has done, that should be put into perspective."

articles.title: A California winery founded in 1981 faces an October 15 buyer deadline after a $12.7 million judgment and Chapter 11 case; court filings put a sale at $3.8M-$6.7M versus $1.4M-$2.8M in liquidation
articles.summary: A California winery that has been operating for 45 years could face liquidation if it fails to find a buyer by October 15, following a long-running legal
articles.body: A California winery that has been operating for 45 years could face liquidation if it fails to find a buyer by October 15, following a long-running legal dispute between members of the family that owns it. Adelaida Vineyards, one of the earliest wineries established in Paso Robles, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2024 after a court ordered it to pay $12.7 million in a case brought by one of the founders' children.According to a report by the San Francisco Chronicle, the winery had approximately $16.3 million in liabilities when it sought bankruptcy protection. Court documents estimate that selling the business could bring in between $3.8 million and $6.7 million. However, if its assets are sold separately through liquidation, their estimated value would fall to between $1.4 million and $2.8 million.The financial problems follow a dispute between siblings Matthew and Kedrin Van Steenwyk over the relationship between the winery and the family's oil-and-gas technology business. Matthew accused Kedrin and other company directors of using money and resources from the technology business to support the winery. A federal jury ruled in his favour in July 2024.Despite the approaching deadline, Adelaida remains open to visitors. The family has also reached a proposed settlement that could help prevent liquidation, although the agreement still requires court approval.How winery became part of family disputeAdelaida Vineyards was founded in 1981 by Don and Elizabeth Van Steenwyk. It was among the first 10 wineries in Paso Robles and later became known for wines inspired by the French regions of Bordeaux, Burgundy and Rhone.The winery sources grapes from estate vineyards spread across approximately 1,800 acres. Its HMR vineyard contains Pinot Noir vines planted in 1964 and Cabernet vines planted in 1973 under the direction of winemaker Andre Tchelistcheff.The family dispute developed after Elizabeth separated the winery from Applied Technologies Associates, the oil-and-gas technology company founded by her husband, who died in 2010.In 2013, Elizabeth arranged for the winery to be sold to KMBG for $3.1 million, without an initial cash payment and at an interest rate below 1%. Applied Technologies continued to own two major vineyards and pay their farming expenses.According to court findings, Elizabeth breached her fiduciary duty when KMBG missed its first two payments and Applied Technologies failed to take action over the defaults.Why Matthew Van Steenwyk went to courtIn 2016, Kedrin became successor trustee of her parents' trust after her mother developed serious cognitive problems, according to court filings. This gave her control over Applied Technologies and KMBG. She also became the winery's majority owner and CEO.Matthew filed a federal lawsuit in 2020, alleging that Kedrin and other directors were allowing Applied Technologies to subsidise Adelaida.His complaint claimed the technology company provided accounting, legal and IT services to the winery for just $2,000 a month, although those services were worth considerably more. It also alleged that the winery and KMBG owed Applied Technologies nearly $2.7 million for operating expenses.The lawsuit raised questions about grape transactions between the businesses. In one instance, Adelaida allegedly purchased Zinfandel grapes from Applied Technologies for $1,299 per ton and resold them to another winery for $2,750 per ton.In July 2024, a federal jury found Kedrin, Elizabeth and other directors liable for breaches of fiduciary duty. The following month, Matthew was awarded $12.7 million. Additional judgments involving Applied Technologies and its subsidiary brought the combined amount to more than $21 million.Bankruptcy filing puts winery's future at riskAdelaida subsequently filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, describing itself in court documents as “a casualty of a dispute between siblings”.The winery argued that Matthew's efforts to enforce the judgment, including attempts to seize assets and access funds in its bank account, had contributed to its financial difficulties.In March 2025, a bankruptcy judge rejected Matthew's request to dismiss the case or convert it into liquidation. However, the judge warned that the winery's “runway is short” because of its continuing cash losses.On June 10, 2026, the bankruptcy court approved a plan requiring the winery to find a buyer by October 15 or proceed towards liquidation.Can the family settlement prevent liquidation?On September 25, all four Van Steenwyk siblings entered into a proposed settlement intended to resolve the outstanding dispute and judgments.Under the agreement, Kedrin would receive $30 million for her ownership interests in Applied Technologies and other family companies and resign from their leadership positions. Matthew and Gretchen would receive her voting interests, while Kedrin would retain her ownership in KMBG and Adelaida. The agreement still needs court approval.An attorney representing Adelaida's liquidating trust told the San Francisco Chroniclethat the winery had not entered escrow or signed a binding letter of intent for a sale as of October 13. However, the attorney said the settlement had “caused the liquidating trustee to consider alternatives”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pope Leo resumes work in hospital while recovering from surgery
articles.summary: Catholic leader met top Vatican aide, as doctors say recovery proceeding after lung surgery to remove cancerous growth.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has resumed work from hospital as the leader of the Roman Catholic Church recovers from surgery to remove a cancerous nodule.

Leo met Vatican chief of staff Archbishop Paolo Rudelli at Gemelli hospital in Rome, where he is being treated, the Vatican said on Thursday. The top aide handles much of the day-to-day administrative work of the Holy See.

An update from Leo’s personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone and Dr Stefano Margaritora, the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli hospital, said the pope’s post-operative tests remained within normal levels and his physiotherapy session on Thursday involved full mobility exercises.

Leo was going about his daily activities independently, doctors said.

“The chest X-ray revealed good recovery of the operated lung,” they reported. “Overall, his post-operative recovery is proceeding as expected.”

For a second day, the pope celebrated Mass with other priests in a special chapel set up near his room on the 10th floor of the hospital, spokesman Matteo Bruni said.

The 71-year-old had part of his right lung removed after a lengthy operation on Tuesday following doctors identifying a suspected cancerous nodule.

The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

Doctors are still awaiting the results of tests to understand the precise molecular makeup of the cancer, whether it has spread beyond the lobe and whether any further treatment is necessary.

Pope Leo attracted a following of almost one million people at a Mass in Paris during a four-day visit to France last month before announcing he was to undergo surgery.

It is unclear whether he will make his planned trip to South American countries next month.

Asked if any changes to Leo’s planned trip from November 6-17 were expected, spokesman Bruni pointed to Leo’s words on Sunday when he announced the discovery of the nodule and impending surgery.

“Thank you for your prayers for the pastoral visit I will make to Peru,” Leo said on Sunday in Spanish, in a greeting delivered to a Peruvian group. The trip is also scheduled to include Uruguay and Argentina.

Leo is expected to remain in hospital until at least next Tuesday.

articles.title: VisionQuest fans to meet Marvel superhero from Wales, with Cardiff accent
articles.summary: Lauren Morais will play villain Lisa Molinari in the new Disney+ superhero series VisionQuest.
articles.body:
Marvel fans around the world are set to meet a Welsh villain - complete with a Cardiff accent.

Lauren Morais, from the Welsh capital, will play Lisa Molinari in the new superhero series VisionQuest - a spin-off from the miniseries WandaVision.

The Disney+ show, exploring whether AI and humanity can co-exist, also stars Paul Bettany, returning as Vision, and James Spader as Ultron.

Morais said getting the role was a "pinch me" moment and that she was "very proud" to introduce her accent to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales , Morais said she initially auditioned with an Essex accent for the part.

In the fourth round of auditions, she also did a northern accent and American.

But during a reading, not knowing if the Marvel team wanted a Welsh accent, Morais decided just to "go for it".

"I said, 'can she be from Cardiff?' and they were like, 'of course'. So she's from Cardiff now," she said.

Morais will follow in the footsteps of Catherine Zeta-Jones who used her Swansea accent in Kill Jackie, a Prime series which follows a former cocaine dealer who is being targeted by hitmen.

The actress said it was important to hear different accents on screen.

"There's a myriad of accents in the UK and sometimes people forget there's so many sick accents around... I think it's so nice that we've got that representation," Morais added.

She said it was a "pinch me" moment when her agent called and told her she got the part.

"I just exploded! I said 'are you sure? Are you joking?' Then an hour later I had to go to a cast dinner," she said.

Morais recalled being like "a rabbit in the headlights" surrounded by all the stars of the show, but was also worrying about who was going to cover her shift at a cinema in London.

During the audition process she was given time off for the VisionQuest auditions, even though she could not tell her manager what the auditions were for.

She said: "I went to my final Pinewood audition and then went back to the cinema to the west end to finish my shift.

"It's such a dichotomy of worlds and that's what it is as an actor, you're always grafting and then it happens and you're like, what is life."

The character of Lisa Molinari has undergone a transformation from the original Marvel comic book character - known as Coat of Arms - who gains extra arms and weapons from a mystical coat.

In VisionQuest, she is instead given a high-tech backpack equipped with robotic arms.

Morais said co-ordinating the choreography for the fight scenes was "funny".

"I'd be with the fight director who was like 'you just need to imagine that a huge arm is coming out of your right side and just absolutely go for it and imagine where it's hitting.' So I used a lot of imagination on that job," she said.

But Bettany, whose character Vision is an android attempting to piece together his wiped memories and fragile humanity, had some sage advice.

"He said 'you're going to feel very silly while you're doing these scenes, but if you commit to it, it's going to look really sick'. And I can confirm, he was right," she said.

The MCU has seen a Welsh character before - the role of Welshpool appeared in Deadpool and Wolverine in 2024.

Wrexham AFC striker Paul Mullin played the surprise role as a Welsh version of Ryan Reynolds' character Deadpool.

It is not the first time Marvel fans will have heard a Cardiff accent, as Kingsley Ben-Adir, who played Gravik in Secret Invasion, previously told Buzzfeed he looked to Butetown , in Cardiff, when developing the character.

Morais said she was very proud her character had a Cardiff accent.

"I'm just so proud to be from Wales, I love it, that's why I wanted my accent in it," she said.

"I love Welsh people, I love Wales, let's go for it."

articles.title: Green Card lottery latest update: US judge orders Trump administration to reopen 2027 Diversity Visa lottery; registration to begin November 1
articles.summary: A US federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reopen registration for the 2027 Diversity Visa program, commonly known as the Green Card
articles.body: A US federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reopen registration for the 2027 Diversity Visa program, commonly known as the Green Card lottery, restoring a pathway to permanent residency for eligible applicants after the government failed to launch the annual registration process on schedule.US District Judge Jinsook Ohta of the Southern District of California issued a preliminary injunction on October 14 in a lawsuit filed by Red Eagle Law, an immigration law firm that challenged the State Department’s failure to open registration for the programme.Under a revised schedule approved by the court, the State Department must announce the registration period by October 29 and open the entry window by November 1. The department must notify selected applicants by December 3. Registration will remain open for 30 days, according to the court proceedings and information provided by the plaintiffs’ counsel.The original order had required the department to announce the registration dates by October 15, open the entry window by October 18 and notify selected applicants by November 19. However, the parties sought an extension, which the court granted.The ruling requires the department to accept eligible electronic entries and process selected applicants under the programme’s established procedures until the available visas for fiscal year 2027 are exhausted or September 30, 2027, whichever comes first.Why was the 2027 Green Card lottery delayed?The State Department announced in November 2025 that it was making changes to the entry process for the 2027 Diversity Visa programme and would announce the registration dates as soon as practicable. However, it did not open registration on the usual schedule, leaving prospective applicants uncertain about whether they would be able to participate.The delay prompted Red Eagle Law to take legal action against the department. The firm argued that the government’s failure to open registration threatened to effectively cancel the programme for the 2027 cycle.The Trump administration had argued that the delay made it too late to conduct the lottery within the applicable statutory timetable. The court’s preliminary injunction requires the government to proceed with the programme despite the delay.What is the US Green Card lottery?The Diversity Visa programme was established under the Immigration and Nationality Act and provides a route to permanent residency for eligible applicants from countries with historically low levels of immigration to the United States.The programme makes up to 55,000 immigrant visas available annually. Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements, including the applicable education or work-experience criteria, and complete the required application and screening procedures.The selection process is conducted through a lottery. Being selected does not guarantee that an applicant will receive a visa, as applicants must still qualify under the programme’s rules and complete the remaining immigration process.The delayed registration means prospective applicants will have a shorter period than usual for selection and subsequent processing during the 2027 fiscal year, which ends on September 30, 2027.Eligible applicants should monitor official State Department announcements for the registration dates, entry website and participation requirements. They should not assume that registration is already open or that selection automatically guarantees permanent residency.Diversity Visa 2026 updateIn December 2025, the Trump administration paused the Diversity Visa program, citing a review of security screening after a shooting at Brown University and the killing of an MIT professor. The suspected perpetrator had reportedly entered through the DV program. In August, a federal judge ordered the resumption of pending cases. The State Department paused the Diversity Visa again. In September, a court found that the government had been slow to comply with the earlier order. DV-2026 visas had to be issued by September 30 this year as the fiscal year ended. articles.summary: The US Postal Service (USPS) is prepared to handle millions of mail-in ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of
articles.body: The US Postal Service (USPS) is prepared to handle millions of mail-in ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress and decide several key races, Postmaster General David Steiner said on Thursday.“Everybody is engaged and absolutely ready for the next two weeks,” Steiner told reporters, according to The Independent.Earlier this month, the USPS announced a series of special measures to ensure ballots reach election officials on time. The measures include extended retail operating hours at some locations, faster processing, additional delivery runs and dedicated ballot pickups.The measures will take effect on October 24 and are aimed at speeding up the delivery of completed ballots during the final stretch of the election campaign. Steiner said the plan also allows local postal operations to bypass regular processing procedures when necessary to ensure timely delivery.The agency reaffirmed its commitment to delivering all ballots mailed by voters, while advising them to post their ballots at least a week before their local deadlines.The preparations come after the US Supreme Court on September 14 declined to allow the postal service to enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump's efforts to tighten restrictions on voting by mail. The USPS subsequently confirmed it would not implement the measure.The rule followed a March executive order by Trump seeking stricter controls on mail-in voting. Under the blocked policy, states would have been required to provide the USPS with lists of eligible mail-ballot recipients and use agency-approved ballot envelopes featuring unique barcodes.The postal service would also have been able to reject ballots that did not meet the requirements or were linked to voters missing from the state-provided lists.During the 2024 presidential election, the USPS handled 99.2 million ballots sent to and from voters. About 30 per cent of votes were cast by mail that year, down from 46 per cent in 2020.Mail-in voting has become a politically significant issue as Republicans seek to retain control of Congress in the midterm elections. articles.title: NHS England bars trans women from female-only hospital wards under new guidance
articles.summary: NHS England's new guidance mandates that hospital accommodations be based on biological sex, reversing previous policies on transgender patient access to female wards. The rulings follow a significant Supreme Court decision and raise concerns among trans rights groups about patient care and operational challenges in hospitals.
articles.body: NHS England has issued new rules requiring hospitals to allocate single-sex wards and facilities according to biological sex rather than gender identity, changing the previous approach to accommodation for transgender patients and staff.Published on Thursday, the guidance covers hospital wards, toilets and changing rooms. It says transgender patients should be accommodated in line with their biological sex, while their clinical needs, privacy, dignity and safety must be considered alongside those of other patients.However, the guidance makes clear that clinical needs take priority when they cannot be reconciled with the requirements for same-sex accommodation.The changes follow a Supreme Court ruling last year that the terms “woman” and “sex” in the Equality Act refer to biological sex and do not include transgender women holding gender recognition certificates. The Equality and Human Rights Commission has also revised its code to state that facilities must be organised by biological sex to qualify as single-sex services under the Act.Trans groups warn of difficulties in hospitalsTransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance criticised the new rules, arguing that hospitals facing staff and resource shortages could struggle to implement them.In a joint statement, the organisations said the guidance could create operational problems and leave healthcare professionals uncertain about how to treat transgender patients safely.“Forcing trans people into spaces for our sex assigned at birth will never be the most clinically appropriate decision, and would push trans people away from accessing care,” as cited by The Guardian.The groups also accused the government of allowing political considerations to take precedence over patient care by failing to resolve the legal uncertainty surrounding the issue.Separate guidance for NHS staff requires organisations to review their facilities to protect the privacy, dignity and safety of all employees. NHS trusts that primarily provide single-sex facilities may offer alternatives, including individual lockable rooms or mixed-sex facilities with separate lockable spaces.The previous NHS England guidance allowed patients and staff to use wards and facilities according to their gender identity.You use AI every day. articles.title: Shackled Maduro calls new torture allegations ‘false’ in latest hearing
articles.summary: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro insisted in court on Thursday that newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife were “false accusations.”
articles.body: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro insisted in court on Thursday that newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife were “false accusations.” Maduro and Cilia Flores, both shackled at the ankles, were brought to court to face a rewritten indictment that expands from an initial set of drug trafficking charges to accuse them of leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans. Maduro twice defied a judge’s request that he enter a plea to the charges. The former Venezuelan leader replied through a courtroom interpreter that the indictment were based on “false accusations and false testimony.” Irked, Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein took matters into his own hands, interjecting that “a plea of not guilty will be entered on behalf of Mr. Maduro.” Flores was less combative. She said she read through a version of the new indictment written in Spanish, she told the judge through the Spanish interpreter. “I am completely innocent,” she said. “I am not guilty.” They were seized from their Caracas home by the U.S. military in a nighttime raid in January. Their trial will begin June 14, 2027, two weeks later than previously set, according to a schedule approved by the judge Thursday. As they have in the past, Maduro and Flores listened to the proceedings through headphones carrying the voice of a courtroom translator. At times, the bespectacled Maduro, who appeared thinner than in previous hearings, looked through papers in front of him and took notes on a pad throughout. Upon entering the courtroom, Maduro waved to people in the gallery and shook hands with one of his lawyers, Barry Pollack. Flores followed him and took her seat before turning to the gallery to smile at familiar faces in the front row. She also gave Mark Donnelly, one of her attorneys, a peck on the cheek. Pollack said when the charges were announced last week that Maduro, 63, denies them and “looks forward to his day in court.” Pollack agreed with the government’s request to move the trial to June 14. He told Hellerstein the new schedule was “very aggressive” given the new allegations, but added that he’s hopeful they’ll be able to stick to it. According to the rewritten indictment, Maduro oversaw a violent torture system that beat, asphyxiated, and delivered electric shocks to its victims. He is accused of personally recommending torture methods, receiving updates on specific victims’ treatment, and threatening to kill one prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture. Flores, 70, a former attorney general, helped develop the repressive system and ordered the torture of some specific people, the indictment alleges. Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture in January, has been under investigation for years by the International Criminal Court over allegations of crimes against humanity, tied to his crackdown on opponents. He has always denied wrongdoing. Torture is a crime under international law and can be prosecuted outside of the nation where the abuse occurred and regardless of the victims' nationality. But the prosecution of foreign officials in the U.S. is exceedingly rare, having been tried only a few times, including against the son of Liberian President Charles Taylor, Russians responsible for war crimes in Ukraine and a former prison warden in Bashar Assad’s Syria. Earlier this year, Maduro and his wife pleaded not guilty in the U.S. drug case, which said they conspired to flood the U.S. with cocaine. Their attorneys say the case should be dismissed on immunity grounds because they were the leader and first lady of a foreign country. The revised indictment covers allegations of torture stretching back to Maduro’s ascent to power in 2013, when he took over as president from his mentor Hugo Chávez, who died of cancer that year. The couple was scheduled to return to the courtroom for another pretrial hearing on Dec. 17.

articles.title: From Ambani to Zelenskyy, Musk mixes business with politics
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The richest man in the world wants a promotion. Elon Musk has conquered electric cars, rockets and social media.
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The richest man in the world wants a promotion. Elon Musk has conquered electric cars, rockets and social media. He now appears to be auditioning for a job that does not exist on any company payroll: global power broker, with a say in who governs Ukraine, who wins American elections, and who gets to do business in India - all without the responsibility of getting elected himself.In another provocative post on his platform X, Musk on Thursday called for Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy to leave office, delivering the message as Kyiv grappled with restrictions affecting its use of the satellite communications network that has become indispensable to its war effort. “And so the slaughter continues… Time for Zelensky to go,” Musk wrote, echoing President Trump’s demand that Ukraine get a new leader capable of striking a deal with Russia, which has returned to good books in MAGA-land. The intervention came amid a fresh deterioration in US-Ukraine relations after Zelenskyy criticised Washington’s decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports and warned that the move could embolden Moscow.The episode captures the extraordinary evolution of Musk from tech whiz entrepreneur into an unelected actor with the capacity to influence elections, shape domestic politics and foreign policy, and potentially affect the military calculations of countries at war. The world’s richest man commands a formidable arsenal of influence: SpaceX’s satellite network, Tesla’s industrial and technological reach, a social-media platform with 241 million followers and hundreds of millions of users, and the financial resources to bankroll political campaigns. Increasingly, those assets appear to operate not merely as commercial enterprises but as instruments of political leverage.Ukraine’s dependence on starlink has made Musk’s relationship with Kyiv particularly consequential. The network provides communications for troops, logistics and drones, including systems used to intercept Russian attacks. Ukraine’s military and civilian infrastructure have come to rely on connectivity that European alternatives cannot readily replace. Ukrainian officials reported this week that restrictions affecting some satellite terminals travelling at high speeds disrupted drone operations and air-defence capabilities. The circumstances raised suspicions that Washington or SpaceX was seeking to constrain Ukraine’s attacks on Russian energy infrastructure amid Trump’s push for a settlement.Musk denied starlink’s restrictions, drawing a distinction between his company’s commercial network, and Starshield, its military-grade system controlled by the US government. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he wrote, referring to starshield and passing the buck to Trump.Polish foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski, whose country pays for Ukrainian starlink subscriptions, challenged Musk directly: “Hey, big man, are you playing politics with your products again? As your European customers, we are watching you.” US Senator Jeanne Shaheen also demanded an end to restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starshield, warning: “Lives are at stake.” republican congressman Dan Crenshaw compared the US withholding assistance to watching a friend die while holding the medicine that could save him.((Musk’s influence is not confined to foreign affairs. His return as a major republican benefactor after his brief rupture with Trump has made him one of the most consequential individual financiers in American politics. According to recent estimates, Musk has spent approximately $366 million in the 2026 US midterm election cycle, including $276 million since July, largely to help Republicans retain control of Congress. The splurging, particularly if the GOP wins, would give him extraordinary access and influence within a party whose legislative decisions could affect his companies, government contracts and regulatory exposure.Musk himself acknowledged in July that his political involvement had gone too far. Asked by The Economist’s editor, Zanny Minton Beddoes, whether he regretted his role in domestic politics, he replied: “I think I got a little too involved in politics, got carried away, frankly.” His subsequent return to big-money republican campaigning suggests that the retreat was temporary.))Musk’s willingness to use provocative language about political power was on display well before his alliance with Trump. In July 2020, when a critic accused the US government of organising a coup in Bolivia to secure lithium for Tesla, Musk clapped back: “We will coup whoever we want! Deal with it.” The exchange followed the removal of Bolivian president Evo Morales in November 2019, an event Morales and his supporters described as a coup. Bolivia gas vast lithium resources, essential for electric-vehicle batteries, making the allegation particularly explosive. Musk later deleted the post, but its significance lay in the apparent nonchalance with which one of the world’s most powerful businessmen treated the prospect of regime change.Musk’s confrontation with India over Starlink’s delayed entry into the country provides another illustration of how readily he deploys his platform to advance commercial objectives. Frustrated by regulatory delays, he first accused unnamed oligarchs of obstructing Starlink to preserve a “monopolistic chokehold” in India. He subsequently challenged the influence of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, asking on X: “Is Ambani the real boss of India?” He followed up with a sarcastic message beginning, “Dear Prime Minister Ambani,” mocking what he portrayed as the industrialist’s power over the country’s decision-making.New Delhi has rejected the suggestion that its regulatory framework discriminated against Starlink, saying satellite operators were at broadly the same stage of regulatory scrutiny and undergoing security assessments. The dispute is nevertheless revealing. By publicly questioning the influence of a rival, Musk has turned a regulatory and commercial dispute into a contest over political power.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Collapse could be precipitous’: Super El Niño could push coral reefs closer to extinction, UN biodiversity expert warns
articles.summary: A potentially record-breaking super El Niño could push the world’s fragile coral reefs closer to extinction as ocean temperatures soar to unprecedented
articles.body: A potentially record-breaking super El Niño could push the world’s fragile coral reefs closer to extinction as ocean temperatures soar to unprecedented levels, David Obura, chair of the UN’s expert scientific panel on biodiversity, has warned.In an interview with news agency AFP, Obura, a Kenyan marine scientist and coral reef expert who chairs the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), said the developing climate phenomenon posed a major additional threat to already vulnerable coral species.“This year's El Niño layers a terrifying level of additional risk,” Obura said.Corals are highly sensitive to heat and particularly vulnerable to climate change, which is warming the world’s oceans and increasing the frequency and intensity of damaging bleaching events.The developing El Niño in the tropical Pacific could intensify these pressures, putting some coral species at greater risk of extinction.El Niño is the warming phase of a natural climate cycle that temporarily raises global temperatures and alters cloud and wind patterns, increasing the risk of damaging weather events.Global forecasters expect the current episode to be the strongest on record, while sea surface temperatures in parts of the Pacific have already reached all-time highs months before its anticipated peak.Obura recalled the devastating effects of the 1997-98 super El Niño, warning that the approaching event could be even more damaging after several major global coral bleaching episodes.“That this coming event is worse than that, after three intervening global bleaching events ... is a terrifying reality,” he said.Nearly half of coral species face elevated extinction riskObura led a major reassessment of coral health published in the journal Nature on Thursday.The study found a sharp deterioration in the condition of reef-building coral species since the previous global assessment in 2008.“Our results show that by 2020, nearly half of coral species were at elevated relative risk of extinction” with climate change the main driver of this decline, Obura and dozens of other scientists wrote.The review examined hundreds of species on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's (IUCN) Red List, including staghorn and table corals. These species build mineral skeletons that give coral reefs their distinctive three-dimensional structure.The findings point to a significant deterioration in conditions for corals, Obura said, attributing the decline to accelerating warming and the continued absence of effective action to curb the broader drivers of coral loss.“This indicates conditions for corals are worsening significantly... not at all surprising given the accelerated warming and lack of abatement of global drivers of coral decline,” he said.However, the assessment was completed in 2020, meaning it does not capture the full impact of the warming and bleaching events that followed.Record ocean heat raises fears of further reef lossesSince the assessment was completed, global ocean temperatures have climbed to unprecedented levels. The most severe coral bleaching episode on record, between 2023 and 2025, caused widespread mortality across reefs.Obura warned that a fresh assessment conducted after the developing El Niño could show an even larger share of coral species facing an elevated risk of extinction.“It is entirely possible that reassessing the status of corals just after this coming El Nino may show them to have crossed the 50 per cent mark of the proportion of species at elevated risk of extinction,” he said.Scientists warned last year that warm-water coral reefs had almost certainly passed a point of no return as ocean temperatures rose beyond levels that most reefs could withstand.The Nature study also highlighted the implications of projected ocean warming and other pressures, saying they would largely determine when and where conditions became unviable for corals, rather than whether that would happen at all.Scientists warn reef collapse could happen rapidlyObura cautioned that the timing of potential reef collapse remained uncertain, with outcomes varying according to when individual reef systems crossed their environmental thresholds.“When they hit their threshold the collapse of reefs in that region could be precipitous and we don't know if that is five, 15 or 30 years into the future, or maybe this year with the super El Nino ramping up?” he said.The developing El Niño has therefore raised concerns about whether already stressed coral ecosystems could withstand another period of extreme ocean heat.The latest assessment, meanwhile, indicates that the risks to reef-building species had already increased substantially by 2020, even before the subsequent record-breaking ocean temperatures and widespread bleaching.

articles.title: Suspected fly tippers shamed with council's online CCTV photos
articles.summary: Hillingdon Council has shared social media posts showing people allegedly dumping rubbish illegally.
articles.body:
A west London council that says it has "had enough" of fly tipping has begun sharing CCTV images on social media, showing people allegedly being caught in the act of dumping rubbish in public places.

Hillingdon Council described the crime as a "blight" on the borough, and as a local authority, it had "allowed the problem to get bigger".

Cabinet member for community environment and enforcement, Adam Bennett, said the action was a "really good first step" adding: "We really need to up our game on all forms of of enforcement."

He said since its CCTV images were shared earlier this week they had over 850,000 views, received 2,500 comments including information on who the perpetrators might be.

Bennett said the reaction to the posts showed fly tipping was "a really important issue to residents".

Hillingdon Council says it issues a £1,000 fixed penalty fine to culprits, and last month it seized and crushed a vehicle that was linked to fly tipping.

"We've had enough as have residents, of the very small minority of individuals who choose to blight our neighbourhoods and communities by thinking it's acceptable to just dump their waste here on the pavement, on a verge, or on a lay-by."

He said by sharing images of suspects' faces the council was "taking action to try and bring the perpetrators to account".

Bennett added: "If you see your face on social media or perhaps on one of our screens in our libraries, our leisure centres, you're going to think twice about wanting to fly tip again."

Bennett explained that "a certain evidential threshold" had to be reached before identifying individuals online, but said as a council they did not want to "shy away" from the problem.

"If you're going to do it in Hillingdon, we're going to call you out for it, and we're going to take every opportunity we can to penalise you for what is unlawful environmental crime that blights the lives of our communities and all of the hard-working taxpayers in this country."

Liberal Democrat London Assembly committee member Gareth Roberts said he was "interested" to see if Hillingdon's tactics of "naming and shaming" individuals worked to prevent fly tipping.

"We need to use everything at our disposal to make sure that we clamp down on these people who think that they can simply trash London because they're too lazy to take things to the appropriate recycling or dumping sites," he said.

This week, City Hall's Environment Committee looked at how London boroughs are responding to the problem of fly tipping, as well as the overall coordination of the response to it.

Roberts said fly tipping is a "major problem" for London and explained there were nearly half a million incidents, across the capital, last year alone.

"Unfortunately clearing up this mess costs councils money and it costs Londoners money," he said.

"What we need is governments to recognise that there is a particular problem in London. We have more fly tipping than anywhere else and it would be great if they could find a way to give councils the money and the resources and the powers to tackle this scourge which is blighting parts of London."
