articles.title: Ahead of US midterms, voters are frustrated with Trump, want change: Poll
articles.summary: Widespread voter disillusionment and pocketbook anxieties set a volatile stage for the GOP weeks before election night.
articles.body:
Voter sentiment across the United States is increasingly negative towards US President Donald Trump’s domestic and foreign policies, according to a new Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll.

In the closing weeks before the November 3 US congressional midterm elections, 80 percent of Americans polled said the country needs substantial change or “complete and total upheaval” in how it is run, according to the survey of over 1,100 US adults released on Thursday.

Democrats and independents are much more likely than Republicans to want a total overhaul of the country’s direction, the survey found, but even Republican voters are still looking for some change. Slightly fewer than half, 45 percent, want substantial change, while 13 percent are seeking upheaval.

The results point to a pervasive appetite for legislative realignment that poses a risk to the Republican Party’s power as it looks to keep control of both houses of the US Congress.

Fuelled by soaring living costs, everyday economics is driving a majority of the electorate, with 85 percent of respondents saying the economy is one of the most significant issues in weighing their vote in the upcoming election. About eight in 10 registered voters disapprove of how Trump is handling the cost of living, and about three-quarters disapprove of his performance on the economy.

Only about one-third of registered voters overall have a “very” or “somewhat” favourable view of the Republican president, and a similar share approve of his performance as president.

More voters want Democrats to win control of Congress and have a more negative view of Republicans.

Immigration and crime rates are also top concerns for some voters, according to the survey results, with 45 percent of voters identifying them as top priorities, though the two issues are prioritised disproportionately by Republican voters who reference them more frequently than Democrats. Conversely, Democratic voters are more prone to name healthcare as their top priority.

Emerging cultural and technological concerns drew less immediate alarm across the board: 35 percent of voters ranked artificial intelligence as a substantial issue, while transgender issues sit significantly lower at 12 percent.

Healthcare is also considered a top issue for 69 percent of voters, while 64 percent cite the war on Iran as top-of-mind.

Despite their grievances, a majority of voters across both major American parties still value civic engagement.

About two-thirds of registered voters in the survey say it’s “extremely” important to vote in the upcoming election, while about two in 10 say it’s “very” important. Seventy-five percent of Democratic voters view it as “extremely” important, compared to roughly 60 percent of Republican respondents.

articles.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered a bronze ring-signet depicting the famous Lighthouse of Alexandria during underwater excavations at the submerged Royal
articles.body: Archaeologists have uncovered a bronze ring-signet depicting the famous Lighthouse of Alexandria during underwater excavations at the submerged Royal Island of Antirhodos in Egypt. The discovery was made at the site of a palace that once formed part of the Royal Quarters of Alexandria’s Portus Magnus, the city’s eastern harbour.According to a newsletter from the European Institute for Underwater Archaeology (IEASM), published on Franck Goddio’s website, the ring-signet is the first known example of its kind to depict the ancient lighthouse. Its relief shows the monument with iconography similar to that found on some coins dating to the 2nd century AD. The discovery was made during ongoing underwater excavations by the European Institute for Underwater Archaeology (IEASM).What did Egypt’s minister witness during the underwater excavationSherif Fathy, Egypt’s Minister of Tourism and Antiquities, visited the archaeological team aboard its research vessel alongside his assistant, Dr Ahmed Rehema. The visit allowed them to witness the underwater archaeological process during this year’s field mission and see the newly discovered bronze ring-signet in person.The excavation work is taking place at the submerged Royal Island of Antirhodos, where archaeologists continue to investigate the remains of the ancient palace.Why the bronze ring-signet matters beyond its depiction of the lighthouseFranck Goddio said, “The discovery of the ring-signet is even more important as it has been excavated in the legendary palace of the Island of Antirhodos, that once was a centre of power”.Goddio’s team interprets the find as evidence that the palace, seen by Strabo during his visit to Egypt between 29 and 25 BC, had at some point housed offices for administrative functions, including administration of the lighthouse.Underwater excavations reveal architectural remains across the Royal Island of AntirhodosOngoing underwater excavations on the Royal Island of Antirhodos are uncovering architectural remains across an area extending to several thousand square metres. articles.title: Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US election offices
articles.summary: A number of states have confirmed they were targeted by the mailings, including Oklahoma, Ohio and Louisiana.
articles.body:
Federal authorities say they are investigating "potentially hazardous" letters containing "suspicious substances" that have been sent to congressional and state election offices around the US.

The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) said they were trying to trace the "suspicious mailings", some of which were intercepted before they were received.

Authorities declined to say how many offices had been targeted, but several secretaries of state and congressional offices reported receiving the letters.

Coming just weeks before the US midterm elections, it echoes previous security scares involving suspicious mail.

"This FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens," the agencies said in a statement on Thursday.

Delaware's Department of Elections said its office received and opened a letter containing a white powdery substance on Thursday, adding that staff followed security protocols on handling suspicious mail.

The Oklahoma State Election Board and the Louisiana secretary of state both said this week that their offices had received letters containing a white powder.

The Louisiana office was evacuated after a staff member opened the package on Tuesday, but it has since reopened after law enforcement found no evidence of harmful substances.

Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose said his office was the intended recipient of a letter containing white powder, but the USPIS had intercepted it.

Senator Chris Murphy, a Connecticut Democrat, was also sent a letter containing a suspicious substance, but it was intercepted before reaching the office, his spokesman said.

The New York State Capitol in Albany and the Wyoming State Capitol in Cheyenne also received suspicious packages, according to emergency responder scanner feed reviewed by the BBC.

The suspicious mailings come just weeks before election day, which will determine the balance of power in Congress.

Ahead of the 2024 election, vote officials in 17 states received suspicious packages .

A year earlier, suspicious envelopes, some laced with fentanyl, were sent to election offices in at least five states.

articles.title: Pennsylvania house that was scene of mass shooting was ‘filthy,’ filled with bottles of urine
articles.summary: A homicidal family patriarch had become a dominant, isolated, figure inside his “filthy” Erie, Pennsylvania, home before killing eight people.
articles.body: A homicidal family patriarch had become “increasingly controlling” inside his “filthy” northwest Pennsylvania home before opening fire with a weapon — linked to a previous domestic violence allegation — and killing eight people, officials said Thursday. Matthew Stone, 45, died of a self-inflicted gunshot on Friday evening, bringing a tragic end to years of descent inside his Perry Street house in Erie, authorities said. Toilets and sinks did not appear to be working and there were 2-liter bottles filled with urine were all over the house, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said. “Detectives described the home as extremely filthy,” Lorah told reporters. Loved ones painted a disturbing picture of Stone’s dominant role inside that house, police said. “According to relatives, he controlled the family’s finances ... and restricted when family members could leave the residence or spend time with relatives,” Lorah said. “Family members told detectives that his behavior had been going on for years. They described Matthew becoming increasingly controlling after (wife and victim) Michelle (Stone) became pregnant with their first child. Over time, contact with extended family became more limited. Michelle stopped maintaining contact with friends. Our department also had a record of prior domestic violence incident at that home.” In that 2019 case, Stone was arrested for allegedly making threats with a .40-caliber handgun. But the case went away when Michelle Stone declined to help press a case, Lorah said. “A firearm was involved in that case, the same 40-caliber handgun that was used in Friday’s homicides,” Lorah said. “At the preliminary hearing, Michelle changed her original statement and those charges were withdrawn. There were no more recent domestic violence incidents reported to our department. Outside of that 2019 case, Matthew had no criminal history and was legally permitted to possess that firearm.” Chief Lorah and Mayor Daria Devlin pledged to examine city contacts with Stone to find if anyone could have intervened before Friday’s bloodshed. “Were there opportunities to recognize that this family was struggling?” Devlin said. “Were there places where our systems could have responded differently and how do we make sure that families in this community who are suffering and struggling like this don’t fall through the cracks?” The victims included the killer’s wife Michelle Stone, 44; pregnant daughter, Angelina K. Stone, 24; sons Matthew Stone Jr., 21, and Jonathan Stone, 19; sister-in-law Lora Lee Roberts, 37, and her fiend Twila A. Tanner, 51. Two other unidentified children, a 5-year-old boy and a nearly 2-year-old girl who were also related to the shooter, were killed inside the house, officials said. Roberts and her friend Tanner had come to the house when Angelina Stone, who was due to give birth on Monday, asked for a ride to the hospital. “Angelina had been sending messages indicating she planned to leave the family home after giving birth,” Lorah said. “When detectives searched the home following the shooting, they found numerous belongings packed into bags and boxes in Angelina’s bedroom.” Angelina Stone had also filed paperwork to change her last name to distance herself from her eventual killer. “In that affidavit, she described concerns about her father’s declining mental health,” Lorah said. “She explained that she wanted to pursue a career in medicine and did not want her association with her father to affect those plans.”

articles.title: ICE agent driving vehicle that struck, injured Houston man is placed on administrative leave
articles.summary: The Harris County DA has interviewed a key witness who was in the ICE vehicle when it hit Miguel Parra Hernandez.
articles.body: The ICE agent who allegedly ran over an immigrant in Houston Saturday has been put on administrative leave while the incident is investigated, a senior Department of Homeland Security official told NBC News. As NBC News previously reported, a senior DHS official said that multiple ICE officers on the scene at the time were wearing body cameras and ICE is reviewing video of the scene as part of an internal investigation. The DHS official said no decision has been made yet about sharing the footage with the public or with the Harris County district attorney’s office, which is conducting its own investigation of the case. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare told NBC News on Thursday that he’s interviewed a key witness who was handcuffed in the back of the ICE vehicle when it hit Miguel Parra Hernández. The witness “had a front row seat to the incident and everything that led up to it,” Teare said. “We did get a significant amount of relevant details from him.” The witness was interviewed at Port Isabel Processing Center, about 35 to 40 miles from the U.S.-Mexico border in south Texas, according to the district attorney’s office. The Port Isabel facility is historically known as the last stop before an immigrant is removed from the U.S. Teare said his office is compiling all information it has gathered or is still gathering and “in very short order we’re going to come to a point where we present this to a grand jury.” He said that could happen as soon as next week. Teare and Cesar Espinosa, cofounder and executive director of FIEL Houston, identified the witness as José Presa Cañada. “It’s very troubling” that Presa is in Port Isabel, Espinosa said Thursday. “We want to know why he’s there and why he hasn’t been released yet and why they are trying to deport him so expeditiously.” Teare declined to comment on what was said during the interview with Presa. Teare also has interviewed Parra. The Oct. 10 auto-pedestrian collision that left Parra hospitalized with multiple injuries and needing surgeries triggered the investigation that could result in aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charges, according to Teare. The district attorney’s office said it had notified ICE soon after the incident that it wanted to interview Presa. In an email, ICE responded that the district attorney should get to Port Isabel fast because the agency planned to deport Presa, according to the DA’s office. ICE has not immediately responded to a request for information on their detention of Presa and about whether it plans to deport him. ICE has previously said that Parra was not its arrest target on Monday. An agency spokesman said after the incident that Parra ran into the ICE vehicle’s path. The other potential witness who was handcuffed in the ICE vehicle that hit Parra is Luis Delfín Martínez, who is being held in the Montgomery Processing Center in Conroe, Texas, north of Houston, according to advocates and family. The district attorney’s office has issued subpoenas for Parra’s medical records, as well as for records of emergency medical personnel who responded when Parra was struck. Teare, Parra’s attorney Kim Bruno and advocates have been pressing the Trump administration not to deport Parra and the two men in the vehicle and have asked the district attorney and others to protect them. Earlier this week, Teare said in an interview that his office had been in touch with consulates for the countries of origin of all three men and let them know they were ready to assist with their application for visas for witnesses key to criminal cases, known as U visas. “We’re working with the powers that be in a really significant effort to keep them here in this country,” he said then. Teare told NBC News that it’s “pretty obvious” from videos his office has collected, including drone video, that ICE intentionally hit and ran over Parra, an allegation ICE has said is reckless and false. Security video of the incident obtained by NBC affiliate KPRC of Houston shows a white truck facing the opposite direction of traffic on a busy roadway. Parra and another man exit the white truck and run, the video shows. At about the same time, the video shows, another vehicle jumps a yellow median and heads in Parra’s direction. The video then shows the vehicle, which is not marked, swerving left toward Parra’s path, in front of a truck stopped in a shopping center. When the parked truck leaves, a man can be seen lying on the pavement behind the ICE vehicle, the video shows. Teare sought to download data from the ICE vehicle while it was still at the scene of the collision, but an agent drove the car away. Driving the car may have automatically erased critical data, said Teare, who led the Harris County district attorney’s office’s vehicular crimes division for several years.

articles.title: Mother of Henry Nowak killer could be deported
articles.summary: Kiran Kaur was found guilty of assisting an offender and was jailed for three years in July.
articles.body:
The mother of murderer Vickrum Digwa could be in line for deportation from the UK, the Home Office has signalled.

Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for three years in July for removing the knife used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill student Henry Nowak from the crime scene.

However Kaur, who spent several months on remand, could serve less than half of her sentence and be freed around the anniversary of Mr Nowak's death under the Government's early release scheme, ITV News reported.

The Home Office and Ministry of Justice declined to comment on individual cases, but said: "We will always seek to deport foreign criminals at the first opportunity."

Kaur, who is an Indian national, could be eligible for the government's deportation scheme.

She is also appealing against her sentence, with a hearing scheduled at the Court of Appeal on 5 November.

Kaur's son Digwa was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on 1 June for the murder of the 18-year-old student, after falsely claiming Mr Nowak had racially abused him in Southampton on 3 December.

Some 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to be released in stages over the next year, down from 6,000 after ministers intervened to exempt rapists and the most serious child sex offenders.

Ministers say the expanded early release scheme is needed to prevent the justice system from collapsing, after a summer when the issue dominated news headlines.

Some 650 criminals were this week released from prisons around the country under the scheme, less than two weeks after 700 were set free early.

The Home Office said: "Our thoughts remain with the family and friends of Henry Nowak, whose life was cruelly cut short in a horrific act of violence."

Sentencing Kaur in July, Judge William Mousley KC told her "a responsible parent would have challenged their son" and asked their child to "do the right thing".

He continued: "You took the knife and put it at home with other weapons in your son's bedroom."

By putting it among "a larger collection of ceremonial and other weapons" it would have "helped to conceal what it had been used for" because she wanted him "to avoid being caught", the judge said.

He acknowledged that Kaur was unlikely to reoffend and said her motive was "mistakenly, to protect your son rather than for any personal gain".

He added: "However, the seriousness of your offending, requires you to be punished and others who might find themselves in a similar situation to be deterred from doing as you did."

Digwa gave the knife to his mother and it was later found by police at their family home along with more than 20 other weapons.

Prosecutor Nicholas Lobbenberg described Kaur's actions as "criminality of the highest order" and her role as "crucial" when it came to removing the knife.

articles.title: Bridgend gang shot at wrong house in revenge attack, court hears
articles.summary: A woman and her son were asleep when two bullets were fired into their home in Pyle.
articles.body:
Bullets were found lodged inside a wall and microwave after a gang targeting a young child fired shots at the wrong home, a court has heard.

A woman and her son were asleep inside the house in Pyle, Bridgend, during the shooting in the early hours of 22 September 2025, but neither were injured.

A jury at Cardiff Crown Court were shown footage of two men firing a 9mm pistol at the property before fleeing on an electric motorbike.

The court heard the incident was carried out in retaliation against alleged drug dealer Daniel O'Callaghan, after the gang believed he had taken drugs worth thousands of pounds from a hiding place in Guernsey.

On Thursday the jury were told the gang dealt drugs, including cocaine and ecstasy, on the Channel Islands and across south Wales.

The court previously heard police discovered a photograph of a child on a mobile phone belonging to one of the men standing trial, along with text messages between them both discussing targeting the youngster.

Kian Darkes and Daniel Clarke, both 21, and from the Bridgend area, admit having a firearm and ammunition in a public place but deny possessing a firearm with intent to endanger life.

The video shown in court, filmed by the two men, show the 9mm pistol being pointed at the house before two shots are fired. It then shows the two men running away from the house.

Doorbell and security cameras in the area capture the two men making their getaway.

A carrier bag containing a hoodie, two sets of gloves and two face masks were later found in a shed at the Bridgend home of alleged gang member Kyle Long.

Gunshot residue was found and DNA tests later confirmed a match to both Darkes and Clarke.

Cardiff Crown Court was told O'Callaghan messaged Darkes after the shooting, telling him he had not taken the drugs.

"WTF is going on. Someone shot a gun. Is that for me? You need to tell me what is going on. I haven't done anything wrong. I've paid whatever I needed to pay. You need to know this wasn't me."

Long, 40, and Callum Pearson, 24, from Cardiff, both deny conspiracy to commit grievous bodily harm with intent.

Jade Evans, 40, from Bridgend denies three counts of conspiracy to supply a Class A drug.

articles.title: Somalia says it will hold elections in 2027
articles.summary: Critics say unilateral decision to call polls is a recipe for more conflict.
articles.body:
Somalia’s election commission has announced that parliamentary and presidential elections will be held in the country next year.

Abdikarim Ahmed Hassan, chief of the Independent National Elections and Boundaries Commission (INEBC), made the announcement on the state broadcaster on Thursday, saying that elections for members of parliament for both the lower and ‌upper ‌chambers are planned for April 15, 2027, followed by a presidential vote scheduled for May 15.

A statement by the electoral body said the vote to elect a president was in accordance with a rule “which stipulates that the president’s term of office is five years, beginning on the date the president is sworn into office”.

President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s second term – starting in 2022 – ended earlier this year, but his government declared a “transition period” through a constitutional amendment in May, despite an agreement with the opposition to hold elections.

Opposition parties boycotted that vote to amend the constitution and have rejected the changes since.

Mohamud is pushing to hold party-based elections to replace a system of electing established clan elders, but his attempts have been opposed by critics, who call his move a power grab.

Former President Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo called the decision to hold elections a “dangerous threat to Somalia’s statehood and future” in a post on X, and urged an agreement with all factions before a decision can be made on the polls.

Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, another former president, who was previously a leader of the opposition, warned that a “contested [electoral] process could lead to parallel elections” and even “civil conflict”, according to the AFP.

Meanwhile, the government welcomed the polling date announcements as an “important stage … towards reinforcing the country’s democratic system” and called on all parties to engage with the process, peacefully “in good faith”.

“There’s no political agreement to hold those elections,” analyst Samira Gaid told the AFP news agency.

“All the processes that the government is starting are leading to further fragmentation,” she said, adding that the government was essentially made up of Mogadishu and “two or three allied member states”.

Elections, Gaid said, would lead to “conflict and more confrontation within the remaining federal member states”.

There was also scepticism in the capital Mogadishu, with some residents calling the announcement “one-sided”.

“Announcing an election schedule through a process driven by one side, and rejected by the opposition, is effectively declaring a new conflict,” Omar Said, a resident of the capital, told AFP.

Speaking to Al Jazeera earlier this month , President Mohamud said the country still faced significant security challenges, despite the al-Shabab group having no presence in the major cities, and despite there being little possibility of the group taking control in Somalia.

Al-Shabab is a Somali armed group that emerged from the Islamic Courts Union in the mid-2000s and pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012. It has fought Somalia’s federal government for years, holds territory in parts of southern and central Somalia, and has carried out deadly attacks, including in Mogadishu and in neighbouring Kenya.

Mohamud said the United States remained Somalia’s strongest partner in the fight against “terrorism”.

He also spoke on Somalia’s relations with neighbouring Ethiopia, describing ties as good, highlighting that Mogadishu does not object to landlocked Addis Ababa gaining access to the sea through a joint agreement to use Somali ports for its economic interests.

In January 2024, Addis Ababa signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland on sea access, which Somalia condemned as a violation of its sovereignty. Somalia and Ethiopia later agreed to ease tensions.

articles.title: Poll shows Bolsonaro with slight lead over Lula ahead of Brazilian run-off
articles.summary: Poll shows right-wing candidate with two percent advantage over Lula going into second round of voting on October 25.
articles.body:
A new poll has found that right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro maintains a slight lead over President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as the two candidates seek an edge ahead of Brazil’s tense October 25 run-off vote.

A Quaest poll released on Thursday found that Bolsonaro, son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, would receive 46 percent of the vote compared to Lula’s 44 percent, a difference within the two-percent margin of error.

Bolsonaro outperformed expectations during the first round of voting on October 4, beating Lula by less than two points despite most polls suggesting that the leftist president was on track for a marginal first-round win. Neither candidate secured a majority that would have avoided a run-off.

The poll, the first released by Quaest since the initial round of voting , shows that Bolsonaro has held onto his lead and remains the favourite heading into the second round.

Lula has sought to rally his supporters after the October 4 loss, holding large rallies that have drawn millions of people onto the street .

While Bolsonaro has remained ahead in the polls, analysts have pointed out that he has not benefitted as much from the elimination of several conservative candidates, whose supporters would presumably prefer him to Lula, as might have been expected after the first round.

Bolsonaro has made progress securing endorsements from right and centre-right parties, however, seeking to consolidate support from conservatives and build a coalition friendly to business interests and a policy agenda sought by investors .

Brazil’s Senate approved a constitutional amendment on Wednesday reducing the country’s maximum workweek from 44 to 40 hours per week without a reduction in pay, delivering a key priority for Lula as the president presses his case to an electorate that is anxious about cost-of-living issues.

“Today is a day to celebrate a historic achievement for millions of workers,” Lula said in a statement. “This means having more time to live, rest, be with family, watch your children grow up, take care of yourself, and enjoy life. Those who work so hard to build Brazil also deserve to have time to live.”

The president also recently banned sports betting, which had caused an explosion of gambling addiction and contributed to surging household debt across the country.

articles.title: Rep Andy Harris threatens to have student journalist prosecuted for recording press conference
articles.summary: University of Maryland's journalism school defended Cat Murphy after GOP Rep. Andy Harris wrongly claimed her recording violated Maryland consent law.
articles.body: Rep. Andy Harris, R-Md., incorrectly insisted that a University of Maryland student journalist was violating state law when she recorded him at a news conference, threatening to refer her to prosecutors during a heated exchange after a debate Tuesday. Speaking in a crowded hallway after an Oct. 13 debate with Democratic challenger Dan Schwartz, Harris demanded that University of Maryland student journalist Cat Murphy stop recording the news conference, arguing Maryland's two-party consent law required his permission. He was annoyed that she defended a reporter from The Baltimore Banner, who had irked him with a "silly" question about why he participated in the debate. "You do not have my permission to record. If you record, we will refer you to the prosecutor," Harris told Murphy, who responded that other journalists were already recording the news conference. PRESS FREEDOM GROUPS THAT BLASTED TRUMP TURN FIRE ON DEM GOVERNOR OVER ALLEGED MEDIA RETALIATION "But you are not allowed to. We are in a two-party state. You are not allowed to," an agitated Harris said while pointing in the student’s face. The student asked why she, specifically, wasn’t allowed to record and Harris continued to grow frustrated. "Because I refuse to give you permission to record," Harris said. "Do you know the law?" The student attempted to have a different journalist hold her recording device, and a separate reporter tried to explain to Harris that the interview was occurring in a public forum. "I’m a legislator. … I actually know the law well," Harris insisted. VIDEO SHOWS MAINE WIRE REPORTER NEARLY BEING RUN OVER BY CAR AFTER CONFRONTATION Murphy then tried to question Harris, who represents Maryland's 1st Congressional District, about the war in Iran. "You’re going to have to take her camera," Harris said to someone in the room. "She is violating the law. In fact, get an officer in here. She’s violating the law on two-party recording. We need an officer." Other reporters repeatedly told Harris they were "in public," but he responded that it "makes no difference whatsoever." LAWMAKER’S STUNNED FACE AND OTHER VIRAL MOMENTS CAP ROUGH WEEK FOR POLITICAL CLASS Harris continued to insist that Murphy needed his permission to record before ending the news conference and walking away. "She’s ruining all your chances to get an answer about anything. See y’all," he said while exiting. "Thank her profusely." In Maryland, the consent requirement only applies to "private conversation," according to the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (RCFP). articles.title: A collector paid about $25 for two colourful jars at a London thrift shop; experts later identified them as rare 18th-century Qing Dynasty porcelain and the pair sold for more than $74,000
articles.summary: A routine visit to a London charity shop turned into an extraordinary discovery when a ceramics collector spotted two small porcelain jars that would
articles.body: A routine visit to a London charity shop turned into an extraordinary discovery when a ceramics collector spotted two small porcelain jars that would later sell for thousands of times their purchase price. According to auction house Roseberys London and reporting by CNN and Artnet News, the pair was identified as rare Chinese porcelain dating to the 18th century and fetched £58,000, including the buyer’s premium, at auction in May 2023. The jars, purchased for around £20, or approximately $25, had initially appeared to be an unassuming thrift-store find. Their distinctive decoration and imperial markings, however, prompted closer examination, leading specialists to recognise their historical and artistic significance.The details that revealed their originsMeasuring approximately 4.5 inches tall, the jars feature colourful chrysanthemums and lotus flowers against a yellow ground. The decorative style is known as doucai, a traditional Chinese porcelain technique that combines underglaze blue painting with coloured enamels applied over the glaze. The pieces were attributed to the Qing Dynasty, which ruled China from 1644 to 1912, and dated to the 18th century. Their bases bear marks associated with the Qianlong Emperor, whose reign lasted from 1735 to 1796 and is widely associated with the production and collection of fine imperial art.The collector reportedly became curious about the markings and began researching the objects before approaching specialists. Their assessment established that the jars were far more significant than ordinary decorative ceramics. The auction house noted that no exact prototype for the particular design had been identified, although comparable patterns were known on Chinese porcelain bowls. This distinction matters because identifying an object’s period, production context and rarity requires more than recognising a familiar motif or imperial seal.Why the porcelain is so valuableChinese imperial porcelain is prized for its technical sophistication, artistic detail and association with the imperial court. During the Qing Dynasty, Jingdezhen, in present-day Jiangxi province, remained a major centre of porcelain production, with its kilns supplying highly refined ceramics for domestic and imperial use. The flowers decorating the jars also carry cultural significance. Chrysanthemums have traditionally been associated with longevity and a prosperous life in Chinese art, while lotus flowers often represent purity and renewal.The combination of craftsmanship, decoration and historical attribution helped distinguish the pair from the everyday ceramics that commonly pass through charity shops. Their condition, however, was not perfect. Hairline cracks and surface scratches were among the imperfections noted in the account of the discovery, potentially limiting their value compared with better-preserved examples. Even so, the objects attracted substantial interest when they reached auction.A £58,000 auction resultThe jars sold through Roseberys London in May 2023 for £58,000, including the buyer’s premium, equivalent to more than $74,000 at the time. That figure represented an exceptional return on the collector’s modest initial outlay. The result also reflected a wider market for rare Chinese ceramics, in which provenance, condition, period and the strength of the attribution can substantially influence final prices.Comparable pieces with similar floral decoration have achieved much higher sums at major auction houses, although differences in condition, design, provenance and completeness make direct comparisons difficult. According to reports surrounding the sale, a significant portion of the proceeds was intended to benefit the charity associated with the shop. The unexpected discovery therefore offered a financial benefit beyond the collector’s own windfall.Why specialist knowledge mattersThe find illustrates how valuable historical objects can remain unrecognised outside specialist markets. Charity shops process large volumes of donated goods, spanning everything from everyday household items to antiques, making it difficult for staff to identify every unusual object. For collectors, the lesson is not that every old jar is a hidden treasure. Rather, distinctive craftsmanship, unusual markings and a design that appears inconsistent with mass-produced modern ceramics can justify further investigation.In this case, curiosity led to research, research led to expert assessment, and that assessment transformed two inexpensive purchases into an auction discovery worth tens of thousands of pounds. The jars’ journey from a London charity shop to the auction room shows how a small detail on an overlooked object can open a window onto centuries of artistic and cultural history.You use AI every day. articles.title: Democratic senator accuses Biden administration of 'completely' chickening out on Supreme Court reform
articles.summary: Sheldon Whitehouse said the Biden administration was "completely chicken" on Supreme Court reform, while Kamala Harris now pushes court expansion.
articles.body: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., called out the Biden administration on Wednesday for a lack of action taken on the Supreme Court and said they were "completely chicken" on it. The Lever's David Sirota asked Whitehouse about what "legitimate" resistance to the court might look like if a Democratic president believed the Supreme Court was "enabling an anti-democratic project." "Well, I think it starts with truth telling and I think the chief executive of the United States has the proverbial bully, the bulliest of all pulpits, and should be prepared to make the argument about what has gone wrong with the courts. The Biden administration was highly reluctant to do that. They completely chickened out. Biden set up that lame committee commission on the Supreme Court and then squelched both Judge Gertner and Professor Tribe when they wanted to describe some of the actual problems at the court so that they couldn't even get that into the report," Whitehouse said. LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES He continued, "The Biden people didn't want to go there. They were completely chicken about all that. They wanted no part of that. And it — really wasn't until the very end, in his last speech after he and Harris had both lost that Biden seemed to have at least somewhat awakened to the fact that the Supreme Court had a real integrity problem." FLASHBACK: DEM SENATOR EMBROILED IN CONFLICT OF INTEREST ROW TARGETED SCOTUS IN ETHICS CRUSADE Nancy Gertner and Laurence Tribe served on former President Biden's Presidential Commission on the Supreme Court. Gertner and Tribe wrote an op-ed in The Washington Post in December 2021, calling for adding more justices to the court after the commission ultimately took no position on adding more justices. DEMOCRATIC SENATOR CLAIMS GOP 'STOLE' TWO SCOTUS SEATS IN 2016, 2020, CALLS FOR EXPANSION Gertner and Tribe were two of the 34 members of the commission, and wrote in The Washington Post, "We now believe that Congress must expand the size of the Supreme Court and do so as soon as possible. We did not come to this conclusion lightly." Whitehouse has been a proponent of Supreme Court ethics legislation as he has argued that the Court has been captured by "right-wing billionaires and special interests." GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED' Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for expanding the Supreme Court during an interview on Wednesday, among other big institutional changes, which included Electoral College reform. "The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her "Baby, This is Keke Palmer" podcast. "I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right?" HARRIS LABELED 'INSTITUTIONAL ARSONIST' FOR PLAN TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM SCOTUS AND ELECTORAL COLLEGE She also called for pursuing statehood for Washington, D.C., as well as Puerto Rico. Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on structural change and promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028. "The odds of Democrats changing the composition of the Supreme Court through a constitutional amendment are near zero, while changing it via statutory legislation (such as expanding the number of seats or imposing term limits) would be extraordinarily difficult. It is a pipe dream. A fantasy. It’s nothing more than something to get their base excited about," Northwestern adjunct law professor Andrew Stoltmann told Fox News Digital in a statement. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE He continued, "A constitutional amendment requires a two-thirds vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, followed by ratification by three-fourths (38 of 50) of state legislatures. Given the deep divides, politically, this is almost impossible. It’s almost silly for Democrats to be arguing that this is a realistic possibility." articles.title: Rally champion Elfyn Evans gets hero's welcome in home village of Dolgellau
articles.summary: Elfyn Efans was greeted by crowds as he drove in Dolgellau with the first minister, after visiting his old school.
articles.body:
New world rally champion Elfyn Evans has been given a hero's welcome by hundreds of supporters at a celebration event in his home county.

The driver from Dinas Mawddwy in Gwynedd drove his Toyota world rally car from the village to a stage in the middle of nearby Dolgellau, before meeting fans for autographs and photographs.

The celebrations ended with a driving exhibition by Evans - where he took First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth for a spin - in the high-powered car around Dolgellau's main car park.

Evans became the first Welsh driver to become world champion , and during the event, he thanked the fans who had supported him since he started his career as a teenager.

Evans said he felt "very lucky and honoured" that the event was arranged, and hoped his success would build "some awareness of the sport".

He added he was taken aback by the cheering from pupils.

"Of course we're used to it on events, but to have it at home is a bit surreal in a way," he said.

"It's a small community, obviously everyone around my age knows me as Elfyn so there's no fuss.

"But maybe for the kids they're only used to seeing me on TV so it's a bit of a different reception."

But he said being champion wouldn't change much in his day to day life.

"Life at home is exactly the same, we still have the same battles to get the kids to school every morning as any other family," he said.

"I will continue to give my best, current or past form won't alter that. I'm still hungry to try and achieve more in the sport and my approach won't change."

Wales' First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth was among the supporters at the celebration event and said Evans was "a true champion".

"To become a world champion is no mean feat," he said.

"He has shown such consistency, such quality over the years - came so close, we felt his pain year after year.

"I had a feeling this year he could do it, and now we are seeing what this means not just to his home area but to the whole of Wales. A true champion a true hero here too," ap Iorwerth said.

Son of former rally driver Gwyndaf Evans, Elfyn - before this year's victory - had finished runner-up in the world championship five times.

The World Rally Championship sees teams battle across multiple events, and various countries and surfaces.

It is one of motorsport's most spectacular and demanding disciplines , taking drivers and cars to the limit across some of the world's most challenging terrain - from snow and ice to gravel, asphalt and extreme heat.

During the final rally of this season in Sardinia, it looked like Evans' main rival and teammate Oliver Solberg would deny him the title once again.

But two corners from the finish line on the last stage of the rally, Solberg slid off the track, sparking jubilation amongst Elfyn Evans's fans.

As part of the celebrations, Evans visited his former school Ysgol Bro Idris earlier on Thursday, where he met pupils and teachers.

Esme and Lois, both 12, said the experience was "amazing".

Esme said she felt "so lucky" that the world champion had visited.

"We're such a small place, but we have such amazing people here," she added.

Louie, 13, met him during the event and "spoke about how much the car was worth and how it felt to see him come first".

He watched him win, and said "it's shows what Wales can do".

Oscar, 13, liked Evans' car, which was on display at the school.

"I'm proud of him for doing what he's done, and he deserves more I reckon."

The school visit was followed by the event in Dolgellau's Eldon Square, where crowds had gathered despite the persistent rain.

Most of the supporters were local, but some had travelled significant distances to be at the event.

When Elfyn Evans spoke from the podium, he thanked his family for supporting him throughout his career, saying his grandfather had "taught me to drive probably far too early".

Wyn Williams from Llanrwst and Neil Pringle from Betws-y-Coed were in Sardinia when Evans clinched the championship.

Williams said the celebration was "the icing on the cake after being in Sardinia".

Pringle added that the evening was "fantastic" and that the first minister's presence "shows what this means to Wales".

"This is for Elfyn, his family and the country."

Heledd Edwards travelled from Talerddig to Dolgellau and described Elfyn's perseverance as an inspiration.

Several members of Elfyn's family were also in the crowd. His aunt, Lowri Edwards, had travelled from Glan Conwy, saying she was immensely proud to have a world champion in the family.

"We're absolutely thrilled, to be honest. He's come so close and been terribly unlucky, finishing second five times - we're absolutely thrilled."

Dolgellau Town Council helped organise the celebration, with Deputy Mayor Nia Wyn Evans, saying: "We are absolutely thrilled and delighted to be able to welcome Elfyn back as a world champion; there's a real buzz in the town."

Evans' victory comes at the end of an era for the high-powered Rally1 cars.

From next season, the world rally championship is introducing new technical regulations which aim to encourage new manufacturers to compete in more affordable and sustainable vehicles.

It will be a new challenge for the drivers and their teams, as Evans sets out to defend his title.

articles.title: U.S. winter is likely to be wetter and warmer, forecasters say, and snow may shift south
articles.summary: Winter in the U.S. looks like it will generally be wetter and warmer, but not necessarily snowier, according to the federal government's seasonal outlook and other forecasts.
articles.body: Winter in the United States looks like it will generally be wetter and warmer, but not necessarily snowier, according to the federal government's seasonal outlook and other meteorologists' forecasts. You can thank or blame El Niño. El Niño is likely to shift weather patterns to bring more moisture, but with it higher temperatures. That should help erase persistent Western drought, but it won't likely make Northern snow-lovers happy, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said Thursday. “This is going to be a winter that’s really difficult for them to find what they’re looking for,” said James Belanger, vice president of meteorology for the Weather Company. El Niño, the natural but temporary warming in parts of the Pacific, generally warms the globe. Although it disrupts weather conditions around the world in dramatically different ways, its effects tend to follow predictable regional patterns, especially when El Niño is strong like it is right now. That gives forecasters greater confidence in what lies ahead. All this is on top of a U.S. winter that has warmed about 4 degrees in the past 50 years, predominantly from human-caused climate change, according to NOAA. The best chance of snow could actually shift south While the weather service doesn't make seasonal snowfall predictions, their meteorologists said much of the northern parts of the country — including the Northeast, Great Lakes, Upper Midwest and Northern Rockies — should expect below-normal snow. The Southern Rockies, parts of the Southeast and Southwest may get more than they usually do. “Listen, even in the winter months, it doesn’t mean you’re not going to have snow. It doesn’t mean you might not have a snowstorm,” National Weather Service Director Ken Graham said in a media briefing presenting the three-month winter outlook. “So it doesn’t erase the risk.” The Northern snow shrinkage is also predicted by private meteorology firms. Salt Lake City is the only big metro area where AccuWeather expects above-normal winter snow amounts. Chicago, Boston, New York and Philadelphia are forecast to get about half or less of their normal winter snow, the firm said. And a White Christmas? Consider a plane ride to the Southern Rockies, Belanger said. Otherwise, “Santa’s gonna find a barren landscape when he returns in late December.” A warmer winter can still pack a punch Part or all of 41 of the Lower 48 states are forecast to be warmer than normal. No states — or even parts of states — are forecast to be cooler than average. Florida, Louisiana, southern Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi are forecast to be near normal. There's equal chance of warm, cold or normal in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, Southern California, Nevada, Wyoming, western Oklahoma, Kansas and Nebraska. And the dreaded polar vortex with its icy blast of Arctic air escaping into the United States? That shouldn't happen as much as most winters, but that doesn't mean it won't happen at all, said National Weather Service meteorologist and branch chief Jon Gottschalck. “It only takes one storm to flip the script, especially for the East Coast cities,” said AccuWeather lead long-range forecaster Paul Pastelok, who said to especially watch for Eastern snowstorms in late January and February. AccuWeather is more bullish than NOAA for snow in the Rockies regions, calling for Denver to have 10 to 18 days with at least 2 inches of snow, which is more than the historical average of 9 inches. The company's overall snow forecast for Denver is still around average, but considerably more than last winter. Drought relief comes with a downside NOAA is forecasting that parts of all of 39 states will see a wetter-than-usual winter, with much of Montana and parts of Oregon, Idaho, Wisconsin and Michigan being drier. “We anticipate drought conditions to improve or end for western portions of Oregon and western Washington state, the Southwest, the central and southern Rockies, the southern Great Plains, the lower Mississippi Valley, and areas in the East,” Gottschalck said. Mike Bettes, a meteorologist at The Weather Channel, said it will likely be too much rain for California: “We'd anticipate numerous, high-impact atmospheric rivers that could bring extensive flooding and landslides this winter.” Atmospheric rivers are long and relatively narrow bands of water vapor. They take water from oceans and flow through the sky, dumping rain in prodigious amounts. Florida and parts of the Southeast should also be on guard for more tornadoes this winter and early spring because of El Niño, Gottschalck said. A record El Niño puts forecasters in uncharted territory Forecasters across the globe expect the current El Niño to reach record levels this fall or winter. Graham, the weather service chief, noted that a strong El Niño doesn't mean its impacts are stronger, but it does make the weather easier to predict. Winter weather expert Judah Cohen, an MIT research scientist, is waiting a couple more weeks before making his forecast. He says an unprecedented El Niño is “a reason not be more confident, but less confident.” “We have no real historical analog or precedent,” Cohen said. “When every meteorologist on the planet is on the same side, I get nervous. We’re not that good.”

articles.title: Hot weather and winds raise California wildfire threat as power shutoffs start
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people in California were without electricity Thursday as utilities tried to reduce the risks of hot, windy weather that could blow over power lines and spark wildfires.
articles.body: Tens of thousands of people in California were without electricity Thursday as utilities tried to reduce the risks of hot, windy weather that could blow over power lines and spark wildfires. In Northern California, nearly 62,000 customers in 26 counties in the Sierra Nevada foothills, wine country and the central coast had no electricity, according to Pacific Gas and Electric Company, which began proactively turning off power Wednesday night. An additional 19,000 customers in Los Angeles, Kern and Ventura counties lost power Thursday, Southern California Edison said. Weather conditions that increase the fire risk were expected to last through Saturday. Some of California’s worst wildfires have been sparked by power equipment, and utilities in recent years have begun proactively shutting off power during dry, windy weather in an effort to prevent blazes. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who faced criticism for her city's response to deadly fires in 2025, said she's directed the fire department to deploy personnel and equipment ahead of the winds. The fire department has also requested assistance from the state’s office of emergency services, she said. “It’s a pretty widespread event of elevated fire weather, so the whole SoCal region should really be on alert,” said Rose Schoenfeld, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service. Dry, warm and gusty northeast winds known as Santa Anas, which blow from the interior of Southern California toward the coast and offshore, are expected, with the strongest winds forecast for Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon. The winds could reach 20 to 40 mph, with gusts from 50 to 70 mph, in the San Gabriel mountains in Los Angeles County and the Santa Susana mountains, which are mostly in Ventura County, Schoenfeld said. Elevated, though brief, critical fire weather conditions are also forecast for portions of the Santa Lucia mountains in San Luis Obispo County. Dangerous conditions began earlier in Northern California, with some communities in the Sierra Nevada and its foothills experiencing strong winds, high temperatures and low humidity starting Wednesday night, the National Weather Service said. The service issued a Red Flag Warning for parts of central and Northern California starting Thursday and lasting through Friday morning, saying any fires would spread rapidly. Such warnings are issued when weather conditions create an increased risk of wildfires. Pacific Gas and Electric Company said Thursday it has notified 90,000 customers in 29 counties that they may lose power. The potential interruption in service to customers from the Central Coast to the upper corners of the Sierra Nevada could last through Saturday afternoon, the company said. In Southern California, the Red Flag Warning for the mountainous areas in Ventura and Los Angeles counties will be in effect from Thursday morning through Friday night. “We are augmenting our staffing, positioning our people and pre-deploying equipment ahead of this weather so we are ready before the first call comes in,” Los Angeles Fire Chief Jaime Moore said. “We are asking residents to do their part, too. Clear the streets, have a plan and stay informed.” In January 2025, the Palisades Fire — fanned by Santa Ana winds — ripped through a hillside Los Angeles neighborhood, killing 12 people and destroying mansions with spectacular ocean views. Authorities determined the Palisades Fire was a carryover from another fire that authorities alleged was caused by a person setting off fireworks. Another fire that burned at the same time in the city of Altadena, in Los Angeles County, killed 19 people and destroyed more than 9,400 homes and businesses. That fire was caused by sparks from an idle transmission tower owned by Southern California Edison, officials said. Schoenfeld said the Santa Ana winds are not going to be as strong as during those fires, when they were gusting 60 to 100 mph. Southern California Edison is considering public safety shutoffs that could affect 245,000 customers, with most of them — 124,000 — in Ventura County, just north of Los Angeles.

articles.title: In the 1990s, Charles Schwab transformed a 2,600-acre Montana horse ranch into a private golf retreat, spending an estimated $30 million to restore its historic character
articles.summary: Every wealthy executive eventually wonders where to escape when the phones stop ringing.
articles.body: Every wealthy executive eventually wonders where to escape when the phones stop ringing. For Charles Schwab, the discount brokerage pioneer, the answer was a quiet corner of western Montana, where a century-old horse ranch offered fishing, dirt roads, and a genuine chance to be an ordinary neighbour. Rather than simply visit, he spent heavily to rebuild the property as a private retreat with a golf course, restored barns, guest houses, and homesites for sale. This article explains how Thoroughbred pastureland became the Stock Farm in the Bitterroot Valley, what it cost, who it was built for, and why it mattered.How Charles Schwab swapped boardroom suits for waders and jeans at his Bitterroot Valley ranch hideawayAccording to Forbes, there was nothing Charles Schwab enjoyed more than slipping away to his reclusive ranch in the Bitterroot Valley, about 35 miles south of Missoula. Forbes described how the discount brokerage founder became Chuck there, a fly fisherman in waders and a regular supper customer at the 20-table Cantina La Cocina in downtown Victor. He drove the valley's dirt roads in a brown-and-white 1980 Chevrolet Suburban and traded his business suits for jeans. Schwab told Forbes, in a telephone interview from his San Francisco headquarters, that he favours Gap denim because of his board role. He was simply a man who valued the ranch first as a private escape from corporate life, where he could go by the first name Chuck.Why a crowded public golf course in Hamilton pushed a ten-handicap golfer to build his own private clubThe Bitterroot Valley had only one drawback for Schwab that the public golf course in nearby Hamilton was overcrowded and pocked with divots. Though it suited casual players, known in golf as duffers, but not a golfer with a ten handicap, which signals a skilled amateur game. Schwab's answer was not to lower his expectations. Instead, Forbes wrote, a man on the Forbes 400 list of wealthiest Americans responded by pouring money into a private alternative. That choice explains why the ranch grew from a quiet retreat into a development with an eighteen-hole course designed by links legend Tom Fazio, scheduled to open in the fall of 1998. Forbes presented the course as the project's emotional centre, the thing closest to Schwab's heart.An estimated thirty-million-dollar restoration of copper king Marcus Daly's century-old Thoroughbred ranchForbes estimated that Schwab poured about 30 million dollars into the 100-year-old, 2,600-acre Stock Farm, the Thoroughbred horse ranch of copper king Marcus Daly. Schwab was intent on restoring the property rather than replacing its character. He planned red barns with galvanised-steel roofs, just as Daly did a century earlier. The club buildings and guest houses would be clapboard structures with pitched single roofs, while log cabins would sit on stone bases. In practical terms, the spending bought a historic look, not a modern resort skyline. For readers weighing the price, the figure is Forbes's estimate rather than a number Schwab confirmed, and the scale of the land, 2,600 acres, shows how much ground the investment covered.What buyers could purchase inside the Stock Farm in 1998Beyond the barns and fairways. The new private golf club offered 350 memberships, which went on the market in the summer of 1998 and were fetching 40,000 dollars apiece. In 1998, 75 had been sold. The development also listed 96 lots tucked into the timber highlands, ranging from one acre to 35 acres and priced between 250,000 dollars and 1 million dollars. Only 12 of those lots had been purchased. Put simply, roughly one in five memberships and about one in eight lots had found buyers, based on the figures Forbes gave. Those numbers show the project was still early in its sales cycle, with most of the inventory waiting for owners.Schwab said it was not about making money, yet Forbes asked whether the buyers would come to MontanaForbes closed its report with Schwab's own explanation. Schwab told Forbes that his life is about investing, which made this project a unique thing for him to do, and that, in his words, "It's not about making money." That statement changes how readers should interpret the figures above. A restoration estimated at 30 million dollars, a golf club with 350 memberships, and 96 homesites might look like a conventional real estate venture, yet Schwab presented the Stock Farm as a unique personal undertaking rather than a profit plan. Forbes headlined its piece with a question about whether buyers would show up if he built the place, which captured the uncertainty of the early sales. As of October 1998, the answer was still unfolding, with buyers arriving gradually and the restoration underway.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Country music's dominant hunting season continues as Koe Wetzel bags a monster bull elk
articles.summary: Koe Wetzel showed off a massive bull elk harvest on Instagram with his compound bow, captioning the post with just two words: "Oklahoma Breakdown."
articles.body: Country music stars are having themselves one heck of a hunting season. Luke Combs, Riley Green, Parker McCollum and Sam Barber have all been getting in on the action this fall. Chris Janson recently told OutKick OutDoors about his own Colorado elk-hunting adventure. And now Koe Wetzel is joining the party with an absolute monster of a bull elk. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS The Texas-born singer showed off his impressive harvest on Instagram Wednesday, posing behind the massive animal with a compound bow resting across its body. The bull sports an enormous set of antlers, and judging by the smile on Wetzel's face, he's pretty pleased with how this particular hunting trip turned out. The caption? Just two words: "Oklahoma Breakdown." Unclear if Koe was revealing the location of his hunt or just happened to be listening to a very good song by Stoney LaRue. Probably both. Either way, that's an impressive animal. The post came just one day after Wetzel shared a collection of music-related photos on Instagram with the caption, "Posted from a remote area hunting elk." COUNTRY STAR CHRIS JANSON ADMITS HE GOT 'A LITTLE COCKY' BEFORE GRUELING COLORADO ELK HUNT Apparently, he was making pretty good use of his time in that remote area. And for anyone familiar with Wetzel's love of hunting, none of this should come as a surprise. During a June appearance on the "Country Outdoors" podcast, Wetzel made it abundantly clear that hunting season takes priority over just about everything else on his calendar. "October to February don't call me cause you're probably not gonna get a nice response," he said. Well, it's October. So consider this your friendly reminder to leave Koe Wetzel alone. The 34-year-old singer has been hunting since childhood, growing up in East Texas and learning to appreciate the outdoors long before his music career took off. In a 2024 interview with Hook & Barrel, he revealed that he got his first bow when he was just 8 years old and still practices archery year-round, sometimes bringing his bows along on tour. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER And this certainly isn't his first gigantic elk. Wetzel previously harvested a big bull in New Mexico, reportedly making a rifle shot from more than 540 yards. During a 2025 appearance on "Country Outdoors," he also discussed taking a bull elk measuring more than 380 inches. It's unclear whether those were the same animal, but one thing is certain: Wetzel has plenty of experience chasing big game. His latest Instagram post doesn't reveal the score of this bull or the details of the hunt. We'd ask him, but he was pretty clear about not calling him this time of year.
